In-distribution fits even predict out-of-distribution error via a one-third scaling exponent.
arxiv-2602-09409:
Chian Yeh Goh and Guillaume Blanquart revisit a 1965 model of Rayleigh-Taylor mixing, where a heavy fluid sinking into a light one churns into turbulence. Belen'kii and Fradkin had proposed a turbulent diffusivity model for the process, and the new paper re-derives it with fresh arguments reaching the same similarity equation. The original work then simplified that equation to extract a key scaling result for how the mixing layer grows.

This paper studies both the full similarity equation and the simplified version in detail. The full equation captures known features of variable-density flows, including uneven spike and bubble growth and a shift of velocity statistics toward the light-fluid side. Comparisons with numerical and experimental studies show reasonable agreement in profiles and growth trends. A global mass correction to the simplified solution closely matches the full solution, showing mixing governed by diffusion competing with mass conservation.
arxiv-2602-09509:
Knowledge distillation compresses a large teacher network into a smaller student, but the capacity gap caps what the student can absorb. Yiyun Zhou and four co-authors ask a sharper question in their 2026 paper. Can a network inherit not just the teacher's structure but as much of its knowledge as possible, and how would it compare with ordinary students from the same teacher? Their answer is InherNet, a network built by inheritance rather than imitation.

InherNet applies asymmetric low-rank decomposition to the teacher's weights, rebuilding a lightweight yet expressive network without major architectural disruption. Singular value decomposition initializes the process, preserving principal knowledge while balancing depth, width, and compression. Across unimodal and multimodal tasks, InherNet beats student networks of similar size. The work points model compression beyond classic distillation toward inheritance.
arxiv-2602-09609:
Video making and editing have gotten better with spread models, yet most systems stay task-single and text-bound, struggling with mixed-media inputs, context links, and varied cases. A 2026 paper led by Jialun Liu offers Tele-Omni, a unified mixed-media design that follows text, image, and sample-video prompts in one model. Editing chains fitted per task further hinder scale and mixing.

Tele-Omni uses ready-made mixed-media language models to parse mixed prompts and infer set making or editing intents, while spread makers make video tuned on those signals. A task-aware data chain unifies mixed-media inputs into a set prompt format while keeping task limits, letting joint training. Covered tasks span text-to-video, image-to-video, first-last-frame making, and in-context making and editing. Splitting parsing from making yields flexible control with strong time smoothness and visual match.
arxiv-2602-10009:
Language models struggle to reason reliably about specific physical systems, and raw simulation traces overwhelm them with fine-grained numbers. A 2026 paper by Sean Memery and Kartic Subr proposes translating traces into sparse high-level patterns first. An unsupervised scheme based on program synthesis learns a library of pattern detectors that annotate traces as short structural sequences.

Human experts can optionally steer the detectors with plain labels such as rigid collision or stretching spring. On a recent physics benchmark, the annotated traces proved far easier for language models to reason with. The synthesized programs stay transparent and explainable, and the paper shows natural-language goals converted into reward programs that search for solutions.
arxiv-2602-10509:
Fuping Zhang and Ruijun Wu prove the existence of cyclic answers to a uneven Dirac equation in a 2026 paper. Motivated by the Soler model, they study a non-coercive nonlinearity on a solid torus, where the spectrum of the Dirac rule first needs clarifying. The lack of coercivity blocks standard variational arguments.

The authors overcome the obstacle with a coercive perturbation. Analyzing key levels and linking structures, they obtain uniform estimates when the rate sits close to the mass. Passing to the zero-perturbation limit yields a nontrivial cyclic answer. The argument extends to suitable scalar external fields, broadening the class of fast-moving models with guaranteed cyclic states.
arxiv-2602-10609:
Shuo He and four co-authors stabilize reward-based learning for large language models in a 2026 paper. Token-level importance sampling ratios swing wildly, and that spread can destabilize policy tuning at scale. Current fixes either freeze one ratio per sequence or adjust tokens independently, ignoring how off-policy drift evolves across tokens.

The team first documents that local off-policy deviation is structurally inconsistent at token level, distorting slope updates across neighbors and risking training collapse. Their method, KPO, models the desired ratio as a latent state evolving across tokens and updates it online with a Kalman filter. Tracking the ratio causally, rather than freezing or isolating it, yields steadier and more strong policy tuning.
arxiv-2602-10909:
Sung Kei Li summarizes how lensed massive stars probe the stellar initial mass function in a 2026 proceeding. A robust initial mass function matters across star formation studies, yet direct measurement stays confined to the local universe by telescope resolution. A newer method reaches beyond: transient lensed stars, single massive stars in strongly lensed galaxies temporarily detectable through microlensing.

Their observed finding rate can break the degeneracy between initial mass function and star formation history in spectral energy spread fitting. That opens a window onto the mass function in lensed galaxies. The proceeding summarizes a contributed talk on the topic, highlighting key results that now support this probe. The work turns rare fleeting stars into number evidence about how stars are born.
arxiv-2602-11009:
Chaos in straight evolution can hinge on the topology chosen, which feels wrong for physics. El-Mehdi Nafia and two co-authors argue that Devaney chaos, framed in pure topology, may shift with that choice and miss intrinsic motion. They propose relative chaos instead, judged against a reference path in a fixed, meaningful norm.

This path-based test does not depend on topology refinements and proves strictly weaker than classic Devaney chaos. The authors show its use on edge-driven reaction-diffusion-transport systems, where it picks out unstable conduct that the older notion may misread. The paper offers a steadier lens for instability in evolution equations on endless spaces.
arxiv-2602-11209:
AI-written code arrives faster than tests can check it. Ziyi Yang and four co-authors present SAFuzz, a hybrid fuzzing frame that hunts stepwise flaws in machine-generated code. It mixes prompt-driven behavioural variety, harness building with problem-specific oracles, and a predictor for resource sharing.

Adaptive sharing and early stopping focus effort where flaws are likeliest. On stepwise contest problems, precision of flaw discrimination rose clearly and time cost fell sharply against a leading fuzzer, with recall held steady. Paired with unit-test making, recall rose further. SAFuzz aims to make testing keep pace with AI coding speed.
arxiv-2602-11309:
Determinantal methods hit a ceiling when bounding tensor rank. Jarosław Buczyński, writing alone, explains the geometric reason for that ceiling using cactus varieties. A known bound says such methods cannot push border-rank lower bounds for a three-way tensor past a straight function of its size.

The paper traces that number, and its analogues in broader tensor spaces, to scheme-theoretic shape. Cactus varieties capture exactly where determinantal arguments run out of power. The work is short and conceptual, giving tensor researchers a clear picture of why a popular method stops where it does, and where new methods must begin.
arxiv-2602-11409:
Agent failures often hide in rare key episodes, not in average confidence. Sina Tayebati and five co-authors offer TRACER, a path-level doubt metric for tool-using agent contact with humans. It combines content-aware surprisal with local awareness, repeats signals, and tool-grounded sense gaps.

A tail-focused risk functional with a max-mixed step risk surfaces decisive anomalies that single-shot proxies miss. Evaluated on tau-bench for failure forecast and selective execution, TRACER improves discrimination and selective scores greatly over rivals. The work enables earlier, more accurate finding of doubt in complex conversational tool use, where looping, incoherent tool calls, or miscoordination trigger failure.
arxiv-2602-11609:
Single-cell RNA data can reveal cell types and developmental paths, but asking a language model to reason over such data directly is still new territory. Yiming Gao and ten co-authors present scPilot, a framework in which a language model converses in plain language while inspecting single-cell data and calling bioinformatics tools on demand. Core analyses become step-by-step reasoning problems the model must solve, justify, and revise when new evidence arrives.

To measure progress the team releases scBench, nine curated datasets with graders for this kind of reasoning. In tests, iterative reasoning lifts cell-type annotation accuracy by 11 percent for one model. Another cuts trajectory error by 30 percent versus one-shot prompting, with clear traces that explain ambiguous marker genes. Grounding models in raw omics data, the authors argue, makes single-cell analysis auditable and diagnostically useful.
arxiv-2602-11909:
Large Audio Language Models are expected to comprehend complex audio much like humans, but current efforts mostly replicate text-based reasoning by encoding audio once, creating an information bottleneck. Daiqing Wu and nine co-authors propose audio-interleaved thought, treating audio as an active thought component for sustained engagement and perception-grounded analysis. A two-stage training framework first teaches models to find salient audio segments through supervised fine-tuning, then rewards skilled re-listening through reinforcement learning.

During thought, the model can re-listen on demand and refine its grasp through a structured generation pipeline, moving beyond one-time coding. On audio comprehension benchmarks, audio-woven thought leads overall in both efficiency and broad use. The authors present the approach as a strong path for advancing audio grasp, arguing that sustained listening, not single-pass encoding, is what audio understanding requires.
arxiv-2602-12109:
Most machine-learning models for solids lean on composition and structure, even though bonding is known to shape properties. Aakash Ashok Naik and six co-authors test whether quantum-chemical bonding scores, drawn from a database extended to about 13,000 solids, actually improve predictions.

Using statistical significance tests, they compare models with and without them on elastic, vibrational, and thermodynamic traits. Adding them improves performance and also yields intuitive symbolic expressions for quantities such as the projected force constant and lattice thermal conductivity. The study supplies a systematic, validated case for bringing bonding information into solid-state machine learning at scale.
arxiv-2602-12209:
Differential privacy trades accuracy for secrecy, but its cost in memory has been far less clear. Alessandro Epasto led this work with two co-authors, proving the first unconditional space lower bound for user-level privacy. The proof runs through a multi-player communication game that ties hard low-memory cases to contribution capping, or tracking users who sway the data too much.

Winning that game needs messages sized to the number of over-active users, and that need becomes a memory floor. Applied to counting distinct items in a stream, any private method needs almost cube-root space for certain error rates, settling an open problem. That gap is exponential against non-private methods, and the same technique also bounds private medians, quantiles, and max selection.
arxiv-2602-12309:
Quantum teleportation sends quantum information using shared entanglement plus classical messages, and its reliability hinges on the quality of shared EPR pairs. Mahmoud Saad Abouamer led this work with three co-authors, pairing entanglement purification with quantum error correction. Fixed-rate codes struggle because purification reshapes the error pattern, so one rate cannot suit every regime.

The team instead uses punctured codes, a family of variants that adapt to error traits and reliability targets while reusing one stabiliser structure. Numerical tests show different punctured codes winning in different regimes, and choosing among them cuts logical error below fixed-rate teleportation. That slack eases the demand on starting EPR quality or purification, making target reliability reachable without swapping hardware codes.
arxiv-2602-12409:
Reaction-diffusion equations with a time delay model spread plus delayed feedback, and solving them across many parts needs care at the joins. Bankim C. Mandal led this work with one co-author, Deeksha Tomer, investigating the Dirichlet-Neumann Waveform Relaxation algorithm for multiple subdomains. The method iterates over waveforms in time, passing information between nearby parts until they agree.

Various arrangements of handoff rules between parts are explored, and a series of tests compares their speed and quality. In this splitting, one side takes Dirichlet data while its neighbour takes Neumann data, and the iteration swaps updated waveforms. That makes the choice of handoff rule a real matter for anyone solving such equations on split domains. A poor rule wastes time, while a good rule keeps the parts in step.
arxiv-2602-12809:
A contact form is called K-contact when its Reeb flow preserves some Riemannian metric, and the three-dimensional case holds special structure. Eugenio Bellini classifies K-contact forms whose Reeb field has a non-periodic orbit somewhere on three-manifolds. He proves that any compact three-manifold carrying such a form must be a lens space, with exactly two periodic Reeb orbits whose periods stand in irrational ratio.

The forms are then classified up to global diffeomorphism by the periods of their closed orbits. Finally, the author connects those periods with the spectrum of the sub-Laplacian, settling a conjecture of Colin de Verdière in the irregular case. The result ties geometry, dynamics, and spectra together in a setting where non-periodic orbits force a rigid shape.
arxiv-2602-13309:
City systems such as bike sharing break the tidy assumptions of most multi-agent learning: the number of active agents changes over time, and actions take different lengths to finish. Sharing one policy across agents adds a second flaw, since agents seeing similar scenes then act alike and crowd each other. Adaptive Value Decomposition is built for this messier semi-multi-agent setting, adapting to shifting agent counts while curbing action sameness.

A training and execution scheme handles asynchronous choices, so agents acting at different times still cooperate. On real bike-sharing redistribution tasks in London and Washington, D.C., the method beat leading baselines, suggesting the design carries over across cities. Yexin Li leads the work with five co-authors.
arxiv-2602-13509:
Hyperspectral cameras see far more than the eye, flagging regions whose spectra stand out from the background, but results usually arrive only after post-processing on the ground. This system moves anomaly detection onto a small drone, running it in real time on a visible and near-infrared push-broom sensor and studying how drone limits affect the algorithm. Because anomaly summaries are far smaller than raw hyperspectral data, they can be sent wirelessly to the ground.

A fast georectification algorithm ties anomalies to map locations, so an operator at a ground station can inspect and characterize flagged areas at once. The full chain, from capture and preparation through detection, transmission, display, and interaction, runs live with relatively low-cost parts. Thomas P. Watson leads the work with three co-authors.
arxiv-2602-13609:
Wormholes are hypothetical tunnels in spacetime. This paper studies round, self-similar wormholes held up by colliding streams of negative-energy null dust, including how such a wormhole might form. Under self-similarity, the Einstein equations reduce to ordinary differential equations. These are solved by computer with edge rules fixing a minimal areal radius, the throat, on constant-time slices. For a large enough throat, geometries stay regular at spatial and future null infinity, while a singular point remains in the past direction.

Formation is modeled by joining three regions, a Schwarzschild black hole, negative-energy Vaidya spacetimes, and the self-similar wormhole, across null shells with the Barrabes-Israel rules. Plain links among throat radius, black hole mass, and shell energy input show an initial black hole evolving into a wormhole, extending a 2004 static model to non-static cases. Yasutaka Koga leads the work with three co-authors.
arxiv-2602-13709:
In a clean insulator, order sets the pattern. Here, strong directional mess in nearby magnetic moments does more than blur that pattern: it builds new topological states that cannot be reached by smoothing disorder away. The team tests the idea with a spinful Qi-Wu-Zhang model, placing a flat Chern insulator beside disordered classical spins of unit length.

They compute the phase map with two approaches: twisted boundary conditions and a topological Hamiltonian approach. When exchange coupling is strong, shifting the mass term moves the system between phases with different Chern numbers. That move happens when zeros, not poles, of the averaged Green's function pass the chemical potential, a route with no clean system match. At strong coupling, a zero Chern number phase stays topologically nontrivial, marked by a spin pattern Chern number that vanishes without disorder. Devesh Vaish leads the work with one co-author.
arxiv-2602-14109:
Kacper Grzelakowski and two co-authors study a 2026 arXiv problem in the geometry of Gushel-Mukai varieties. The focus is plain kinds with a single node, in sizes three, four, and five, under mild broad rules. Blowing up the node links the kind, via a relative Atiyah flop, to a quadric bundle over the flat plane.

The authors name the categorical fix of the Kuznetsov part with the Clifford part of that bundle. They then treat hyperbolic sameness, links to Verra kinds, and birational Torelli for broad nodal threefolds. For fourfolds, a countable union of divisor families proves dense, with rational members and untwisted degree-two K3 parts. A spinor tweak of the conic bundle caps the work.
arxiv-2602-14409:
Haichao Zhu and two co-authors test a 2026 arXiv rule for space thought: learning offers, shape rules. Space sight gauges camera motion and scene form, long done via shape models and physics rules. Learning methods now aid old systems, but whether they should swap shape guessing or serve as parts inside it stays open.

The paper studies a full modular setup where learning offers shape guesses and shape methods make final guess choices. In relative camera pose guessing on RGB-D runs, the team tests VGGT pose and depth offers under varied motion and scene shifts, followed by old point-to-plane RGB-D ICP as the shape decider. The study marks where learning helps most and where shape must overrule it.
arxiv-2602-14709:
Simon Arridge and colleagues survey the Deep Image Prior for computed tomography reconstruction, a method that needs no large supervised dataset. The prior exploits the implicit bias of convolutional networks and works unsupervised from a single measurement, even with noise, turning a network's structure itself into a regulariser.

The survey sets out the standard formulation, key design choices, and tricks against overfitting, from early stopping and explicit regularisation to self-guided methods that adapt the network input. Warm-start and stochastic optimisation speed the computation. The paper gives newcomers and practitioners a full map of a striking idea in medical imaging.
arxiv-2602-15009:
Alam and colleagues give growth conditions that guarantee topological freeness for group actions. They start with a finitely generated group, a non-trivial element, and a minimal action on a compact space whose neighborhood stabilizers are amenable. In terms of growth and decay functions, they prove sufficient conditions for the action to be topologically free.

The results are then applied to the Furstenberg boundary action, yielding C-star simplicity under sub-rapid decay conditions. In the same setting, the paper describes the support of stationary states on the reduced C-star algebra of the group. The work ties growth behavior of group elements to freeness and simplicity in a concrete, checkable form.
arxiv-2602-15109:
Barwell and colleagues test whether galaxy mergers trigger powerful radio galaxies, and whether the answer depends on AGN sub-type. Powerful radio-loud active galactic nuclei drive a key form of feedback, so their triggers matter for galaxy evolution models. The team uses deep Isaac Newton Telescope imaging, joined to Gemini South images, for a 98 percent complete sample of 112 3CR radio galaxies below redshift 0.3, plus a mass-matched control sample.

Results show strong evidence that triggering differs across sub-types. High-excitation galaxies show a 62 percent rate of morphological disturbance, an excess over controls, fitting merger-driven triggering. Low-excitation galaxies show only 36 percent, matching controls, suggesting a different main trigger such as gas accretion from hot X-ray haloes. Among FRII sources, high-excitation objects favor disturbed shapes more than low-excitation ones, arguing against low-excitation FRII sources being merely switched-off high-excitation objects.
arxiv-2602-15309:
Atalla and colleagues present OSCAR, a wasp-inspired pod turning wasp transport into drive for colon exams. Moving within the slick colon stays a big hurdle. OSCAR sets the wasp-inspired move rhythm through a spring cam pushing twelve ring pads in timed order.

Tweaking the move curve to lengthen pullback versus push, the pod makes set grip bias making net push. A Kelvin-Voigt model holds stretchy stick-slip contact between pads and gut, tying phase gap to mean push and pad timing to push calm. Force tests in pig colon showed a mean pull of eighty-five hundredths Newton, nearly fitting the model. Tests showed push is speed-free and grows straight with phase gap, fitting guesses. In travel tests, OSCAR hit about three mm per second, fitting entry times. Joining grip bias with a forecast model, OSCAR gives managed push at low loads, allowing safer travel.
arxiv-2602-15409:
Montesi and colleagues offer a formal work of Hennessy-Milner Logic, a basic logic for step systems, for the Lean shelf. Their work covers the grammar, truth link, and meaning sense of HML, as well as a full meta-work with the Hennessy-Milner rule: twin behavior matches view match for image-finite step systems.

Their work stresses breadth and reuse: it is tunable over any step systems, and defs plug with CSLib's base such as the formal work of twin behavior. Checks use Lean's auto help, chiefly the grind tool. All code is openly open in CSLib and can be easily used by systems that use its LTS API.
arxiv-2602-15609:
Bravo-Gaete and colleagues study spinning particles on periodic orbits around black holes in Deser-Woodard nonlocal gravity. Using the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon equations with the Tulczyjew spin condition, they derive orbital equations for equatorial motion and impose a timelike rule to bar superluminal paths. They compare nonlocal effects on the effective potential and on the innermost stable circular orbit against the classic Schwarzschild case.

Waveforms show clear phase shifts: raising the nonlocal parameter zeta delays phase, while raising b advances it. A one-year simulation of an extreme mass ratio inspiral tests those shifts. At b equal to two and zeta near ten to the minus six, the waveform mismatch against Schwarzschild reaches the distinguishable threshold of 0.0125. The result gives observers a concrete basis for telling nonlocal gravity apart from general relativity.
arxiv-2602-15709:
Lichev and colleagues analyse the depth of depth-weighted trees. Such a tree grows from a root, and each new vertex attaches to a parent with chance proportional to a weight function of the parent depth. The work gives a systematic account of typical depth across weight regimes: convergent, periodic, slowly growing, and super-exponentially growing functions.

For bounded or exponentially growing weights, the team pins typical depth down to a multiplicative constant. That result confirms and strengthens a conjecture of Leckey, Mitsche, and Wormald. Probabilists gain precise analytic expressions for how deep such trees typically grow, and how that depth shifts as the weight function changes shape.
arxiv-2602-15809:
Tian and colleagues present a Decision Quality Evaluation Framework built and deployed at Pinterest for content safety at scale. Online platforms need robust systems to enforce content safety policies. A key part is judging review calls made by human agents and large language models. That judging is hard due to trade-offs between cost, scale, and trust, plus shifting policy tangle.

The frame centres on a high-trust Golden Set curated by subject matter experts, serving as a ground truth benchmark. An auto smart sampling pipe uses tilt scores to expand data set reach fast. Uses include testing cost-performance trade-offs of various language model agents, data-driven prompt tuning, handling complex policy change, and guarding soundness of policy content rate metrics via ongoing checks. The frame enables a shift from gut assessments to a data-driven and counted practice for managing content safety systems.
arxiv-2602-15909:
Zhang and colleagues built Resp-Agent, a self-run multimodal system for lung sound generation and disease diagnosis. Lung sound work by deep learning faces two blocks. Turning signals into spectrograms drops brief sound events and clinical context, and training data is scarce with stark class imbalance.

A central controller, Thinker-A2CA, spots weak diagnoses and queues targeted synthesis in a loop. A Diagnoser weaves clinical text with audio tokens through broad attention and sparse audio anchors, catching long-range context and millisecond transients. A Generator adapts a text-only language model to make hard cases, splitting disease content from sound style. Resp-229k, a set of 229k recordings with distilled clinical notes, backs the work. Tests beat prior methods across varied settings, lifting robustness under scarce and skewed data.
arxiv-2602-16009:
Anugu and colleagues report the overhaul of the CHARA Array delay lines, the moving carts that equalize light paths between telescopes as Earth turns and the air shimmers. CHARA, at Mount Wilson, resolves stars, binaries, disks, and active galactic nuclei at long baselines, but its legacy control system had run for over two decades and spare parts were drying up.

From mid 2021 through 2024, the team replaced the aging VME architecture with a hybrid FPGA and Linux system. The upgrade matches the old tracking error near twelve nanometres while reaching a control bandwidth that supports fringe tracking across red and infrared bands. Early faults such as metrology jitter and vibration driven visibility loss were diagnosed and fixed, and plans now aim at baselines near a kilometre.
arxiv-2602-16209:
Neural operators learn solutions of partial differential equations in a resolution-invariant, data-driven way. They often grow unstable during multi-layer iteration and long-horizon rollout. Jiaquan Zhang and coauthors trace that instability to unconstrained Euclidean latent space updates. Those updates violate shape and conservation laws. Their method, Manifold Constraining based on Lie group, or MCL, constrains manifolds with low-rank Lie algebra parameterization. It performs group action updates on latent representations.

MCL acts as an efficient plug-and-play module that enforces shape inductive bias in existing neural operators. Tests on varied partial differential equations, including one-dimensional Burgers and two-dimensional Navier-Stokes, show relative prediction error falling by roughly a third to a half. The cost is just over two percent more parameters. The approach thus offers a scalable route to better long-term prediction fidelity. It restores geometric constraints that standard updates ignore.
arxiv-2602-16309:
Jakub Breier and coauthors investigate how number representations affect electromagnetic fault injection attacks on embedded deep learning models. Fault injection attacks on embedded neural network models are a potent threat, and prior work studied model resilience from various viewpoints. No comprehensive study had evaluated how number representations used for model parameters influence success of such attacks. The authors test four representations: two floating-point formats and two integer formats.

They deploy four common image classifiers on an embedded memory chip and use a low-cost fault injection platform to trigger faults. They also characterize injected fault patterns across formats. Results show floating-point representations exhibiting almost complete accuracy degradation after a single fault injection, while integer representations offer better resistance overall. In particular, the eight-bit representation on a relatively large network retains substantial top-one and top-five accuracy.
arxiv-2602-16409:
Pavan A. Uttarkar leads eleven coauthors observing the most active repeating fast radio burst. Fast radio bursts are bright, energetic radio pulses from outside our galaxy. Some sources repeat while most do not, and most repeating sources repeat only rarely. None was previously studied over wide bandwidths needed to separate emission physics from distortions caused by intervening ionised gas.

Using an ultrawideband system, the team detected five thousand five hundred and twenty-six bursts from FRB 20240114A, revealing extreme spectral and temporal changes. The bursts show longer-term broadband shifts in central emission frequency over months, plus narrowband bursts correlating on timescales from milliseconds to minutes. Those fit a source magnified by foreground plasma lenses, possibly in a turbulent medium around the source. The extreme example highlights how plasma lenses shape burst traits and may explain the diversity in activity and energetics across the fast radio burst population.
arxiv-2602-16509:
Roger Tribe and Oleg Zaboronski study entrance laws for systems of instantaneously annihilating or coalescing Brownian motions on the line. Such systems let particles vanish on meeting or merge into one, and the paper asks which entrance laws such a process can have.

The authors show that the extreme points of the set of entrance laws are Pfaffian point processes at all times, and they identify the kernels of these processes. The result pins down the extreme entrance laws for this process, giving readers the exact kernels behind the extreme cases.
arxiv-2602-17009:
Nikunj Gupta and co-authors propose Action Graph Policies, modeling action co-dependencies in multi-agent reinforcement learning. Coordinating actions is the most basic form of cooperation in multi-agent reinforcement learning. Good decentralized decision-making often depends not only on good individual actions, but on picking compatible actions across agents to sync behavior, avoid conflicts, and meet global constraints.

Action Graph Policies model dependencies among agents' available action choices, building coordination contexts that let agents base decisions on global action dependencies. In theory, the policies induce a richer joint policy compared to fully independent policies. They can realize coordinated joint actions provably more optimal than greedy execution even from centralized value-decomposition methods. In tests, the policies achieve eighty to ninety-five percent success on canonical coordination tasks with partial observability and anti-coordination penalties, where other multi-agent methods reach only ten to twenty-five percent.
arxiv-2602-17209:
Alejandro Flores led a five-author team designing a layered sky network for remote healthcare computing. Field clinics and medical internet-of-things devices in remote places generate tasks that need computing power they lack. The paper studies a hierarchical non-terrestrial network: a high-altitude platform offers local edge services to ground medical devices, while a low-Earth-orbit satellite bridges to a distant cloud server through a ground gateway.

Each tier charges for its spectrum or compute and seeks its own best payoff, with a local delay cost pushing prompt handling. The authors derive the optimal per-task price at each tier, the offloading rules those prices induce, and the matching bandwidth allocation. The framework shows how pricing and offloading can be tuned tier by tier for far-flung medical deployments.
arxiv-2602-17309:
Stavros Konstantinidis, writing alone, unifies three relaxed code families under one definition. A prefix code forbids any word being a proper prefix of another. Recent work relaxed that rule to allow a word to prefix at most a fixed margin of other words. That creates k-prefix-free, k-suffix-free, and k-infix-free languages. The paper unifies these three classes in two ways: through partial orders and through transducers.

That unification pays off broadly: for any known class of code-related languages definable by transducers, one immediately gets a marginal version of that class. Building on the techniques of Ko, Han, and Salomaa, the author also discusses two problems for marginal classes: uniform satisfaction and maximality. The paper maps which questions the unified view answers and which remain open.
arxiv-2602-17509:
The CMS Collaboration presents a measurement of event shape variables using charged particles inside jets in proton-proton collisions at thirteen teraelectronvolts. Event shape variables, built from the four-momenta of final-state objects in an event, react keenly to quantum chromodynamics predictions in multijet production. The study takes in five such variables, using proton-proton collision data from the CMS detector in twenty sixteen to twenty eighteen, at thirteen teraelectronvolts, matching one hundred thirty-eight inverse femtobarns.

The variables are gauged from charged particles inside jets. After detector effects are corrected, their spreads are set beside predictions from several multijet models. The data match several theory predictions broadly, leaving room to sharpen our grasp of quantum chromodynamics at varied energy scales.
arxiv-2602-17609:
Marouan Mizmizi and team design a phone-centered sensing method to hold handheld devices within exposure limits. Rules cap how much radio energy a body may absorb. Today's proximity sensors give only a yes-or-no signal, forcing cautious power cuts that hurt link quality. A true distance measure would allow proportional control.

Their integrated sensing and communication approach reuses the uplink waveform for sensing. Natural hand motion forms a virtual aperture sharp enough to locate the body. Since the hand's path is unknown, an autofocus algorithm based on extended Kalman filtering tracks the path and corrects errors from phase data. Simulations at a high frequency band reach centimeter-level accuracy with realistic sensor parameters.
arxiv-2602-17709:
Lin Huang and team present UBio-MolFM, a universal foundation model for bio-systems built to serve as a computational microscope for life's machinery. All-atom molecular simulation faces a hard trade between quantum-mechanical accuracy and biological scale. The new frame aims to bridge that gap.

Three innovations work together. A large bio-specific data set, UBio-Mol26, mixes bottom-up enumeration with top-down sampling of native protein settings, reaching twelve hundred atoms. A linear-scaling equivariant transformer, E2Former-V2, captures non-local physics with about four times higher inference throughput on large systems. A three-stage curriculum moves from energy starts to energy-force consistency. Benchmarks show ab initio-level fidelity on large, out-of-distribution biomolecular systems up to fifteen hundred atoms.
arxiv-2602-17909:
Amirhosein Javadi and team show that a single image plus multimodality suffices for novel view synthesis. Diffusion-based approaches perform for novel view synthesis by conditioning models on monocular depth geometry. View quality and consistency are limited by depth estimate trust, fragile under low-texture, adverse weather and block-heavy conditions.

The paper shows sparse multimodal range measurements offer a simple remedy. A multimodal depth rebuild frame leverages sparse range sensing data, such as radar or LiDAR, to produce dense depth maps for shape conditioning in novel view synthesis. Depth is modeled in an angular domain using a Gaussian Process, enabling efficient inference with uncertainty scored. Rebuilt depth and uncertainty replace those tools as a drop-in for rendering pipelines, with no changes to the model. Tests on driving scenes show replacing vision-only depth with sparse range-based rebuild improves shape match and visual quality in novel-view video.
arxiv-2602-18109:
Rong Fu and six co-authors built TempoNet, a scheduler that uses learning to meet tight deadlines on many processors. Their 2026 paper pairs a Transformer model, which can weigh tasks in any order, with a value-learning method that scores choices. A special step turns time left before each deadline into learned codes, which steadies learning and marks how urgent each task is.

A fast attention design scans whole task sets in near-linear time, with answers in under a millisecond, and a mapping step turns scores into processor slots. Tests on factory-style traces and large multi-processor setups beat both rule-based schedulers and earlier learned ones on deadline success, with steadier training. Extra checks cover stress, hardware runs, and kernel tests. The paper offers a workable path for learned choice-making in fast, high-volume scheduling.
arxiv-2602-18209:
R. Cesaroni and eight co-authors map a young ionized bubble around massive stars in the cloud G31.41+0.31. Their 2026 paper, part of the GUAPOS project, uses ALMA's full three-millimeter band plus VLA continuum data to probe the region's gas. Ionized zones around OB stars form early, yet few have been mapped in both ionized and neutral gas at fine detail.

Fitting many hydrogen lines and molecular tracers with a model that allows non-equilibrium effects, the team finds electron temperatures mostly between five and six thousand degrees. Densities run between two thousand five hundred and seven thousand five hundred per cubic centimeter. The pattern and velocity field point to a comet-shaped bubble expanding away from us toward the northwest. Nearby molecular gas still falls toward the bubble's peak, and its pressure seems to pen the ionized gas in from the southeast.
arxiv-2602-18509:
Holly Jackson and three co-authors recover depth from blurred images by direct optimization. Their 2026 paper notes a reasonable forward model for blur exists from optical physics, yet recovering depth from defocused images remains a computationally hard optimization problem. With contemporary methods and reasonable computing power, a global optimization approach becomes feasible.

The approach rests on alternating minimization. With the depth map fixed, the forward model stays linear in the all-in-focus image. Holding the all-in-focus image fixed, each pixel's depth can be computed independently, enabling embarrassingly parallel work. Alternating convex optimization with parallel grid search effectively solves depth-from-defocus at higher resolutions than today's deep learning methods. The team demonstrates the approach with benchmark datasets covering synthetic and real defocus blur, showing promising results compared with prior work.
arxiv-2602-18609:
Siddhant Sen and three co-authors compare two edges of galaxy clusters. Their 2026 paper notes dark matter and gas edges are marked by the splashback radius and accretion shock, expected theoretically to coincide at outskirts. Hydrodynamic cosmological simulations show significant displacement between them. Using the IllustrisTNG suite, the team investigates the statistical relationship between splashback and shock surfaces in eight hundred twelve halos.

They map the full angular distribution of both edges and examine correlations with halo properties, using a dispersion measure for splashback and entropy distance for shock location. Despite various boundary definitions, an offset persists, with shock-to-splashback radius ratios near one point three to two depending on method, mostly along void directions. Redshift evolution shows the edges are not necessarily distinct early. During mergers, gas sheds energy and resists contraction through pressure, unlike collisionless dark matter, producing the observed offset.
arxiv-2602-18709:
Robots that map a room need both geometry and meaning. They must know where surfaces are, and which object is which, even seen from far apart. Tingyang Xiao, with eight co-authors, presents IRIS-SLAM in 2026. It is a semantic mapping system that unifies those two jobs in one representation. That representation builds on a geometry foundation model extended with instance information.

The same model predicts dense geometry and cross-view instance embeddings. Matching across views and recognising a place again, known as loop closure, both draw on viewpoint-agnostic semantic anchors. That shared basis bridges geometric reconstruction and open-vocabulary mapping. Tests show clear gains over leading methods. Gains are largest in map consistency and in reliable loop closure over wide baselines.
arxiv-2602-18809:
Future electron-proton colliders could produce top quark pairs, but predicting that rate at the kinematic edge needs a careful bound. G. R. Boroun, writing alone in 2026, analyses the ratio of structure functions for deep inelastic top pair production at fixed centre-of-mass energy and momentum transfer, using collinear factorisation.

A compact formula for that ratio helps extract a limit for the top structure function from data. The reduced cross section at the limit then sets a limit value for top production at LHeC and FCC-eh energies. A Bjorken scaling modification improves the quantity at low momentum transfer. The dipole cross section is also examined across dipole sizes, suggesting limited prospects for observing top saturation, and the Higgs probability in photon-gluon interactions is compared with the gluon-gluon process.
arxiv-2602-18909:
Cells often divide while squeezed by nearby structures, yet how the squeeze shapes division forces is unclear. Amit Singh Vishen, writing alone in 2026, builds a minimal mechanical theory of confined cell division. The cell is modelled as one incompressible volume bounded by an interface under effective isotropic tension.

The squeeze restricts which furrow shapes are mechanically admissible. As the furrow radius shrinks, it hits a squeeze-induced minimum. Beyond that point, further ingression does not change the interface shape. Pressure and axial force then saturate. One geometric mechanism unifies rigid, soft, and strong three-dimensional squeeze. After rescaling by the apt geometric scale, cells of different size and tension collapse onto one universal curve. Geometry thus bounds mitotic force and pressure, while material traits and active forces pick the point used. Shape sets the ceiling. Forces then pick a spot below it.
arxiv-2602-19009:
School choice usually assumes each school ranks applicants in one priority order. Haoyu Song, with two co-authors, studies a many-to-one matching model in 2026 where schools rank applicants on several rankings instead of one priority order. Each school's evaluation is modelled with social choice criteria, reflecting its internal ranking process.

A choice counts as acceptable when evaluators rank a person above a set percentile of the accepted cohort. Stability is then defined by who counts. Accepted people must receive strong support, while rejected people receive at most weak support. Since exact acceptance and stability may not exist, approximately stable outcomes are constructed using a new balance concept. It combines matching with a Lindahl equilibrium, defined over ordinal preferences, giving a flexible, equilibrium-based frame for committee-based matching markets.
arxiv-2602-19109:
How does a language model finalise a three-digit sum? Yao Yan, writing alone in 2026, traces that process in Meta-Llama-3-8B under a one-token readout. Causal patching and attention ablations locate a sharp boundary near layer seventeen. Beyond it, the decoded sum rests almost entirely on the last input token. Late-layer self-attention becomes largely dispensable.

In that post-routing regime, digit-direction dictionaries shift with next-higher-digit context. Yet they stay related by a near-orthogonal map inside a shared low-rank subspace. Causal digit editing confirms the geometry. Naive cross-context transfer fails. Rotating directions via the learned map restores exact counterfactual edits. Negative controls do not recover. Arithmetic answers thus finalise through rotation-structured directions after routing ends.
arxiv-2602-19309:
Language models can bargain, but a fixed plan learned offline may miss what an opponent reveals round after round. Xiangyu Liu and three co-authors treat extra computation at run time as the way to adapt. It builds smooth fictitious play, a classic game-theory learning rule, into the model's run. A helper model of the opponent learns in context to copy the opponent's average past behavior, forming beliefs about what comes next.

For replies, the method improves best-of-N sampling by testing candidate replies against that opponent model. Tests on two kinds of repeated deal-making games show clear gains over baselines as play continues. The appeal is a sound way to adapt online in strategic settings, with no parameter updates at all, using only more computation when deciding.
arxiv-2602-19909:
Evaluating multi-loop scattering amplitudes hinges on reducing Feynman integrals by parts, a step that can explode into huge equation systems when numerators or propagators carry high powers. A 2026 arXiv paper by Sid Smith, working alone, presents a new algorithm that avoids that explosion.

Instead of building a large middle system, the algorithm applies direct reduction rules tied to syzygies. The author demonstrates it on demanding cases. These include high-rank integrals for a double-box case with an external mass and for a massless pentabox case. The author also reports much faster reduction for spinning black-hole binary amplitudes. The paper also presents LoopIn, a modular toolkit for automating multi-loop calculations that can use these techniques.
arxiv-2602-20009:
Some community cooperation projects spark lasting participation. Others leave local social life untouched. The difference may lie in how taking part itself is organized. A 2026 arXiv paper by Giorgia Sampò and two co-authors introduces a mixed-method framework for judging the social impact of such projects in developing countries.

The authors argue outcomes hinge on participation architecture. That means simple, visible routines: onboarding help, template-based tasks, and light tracking of inputs and benefits. Such routines create easy entry points and route work across groups without heavy hierarchy. Their framework, Project Intervention Response Analysis, compares observed community networks with what-if networks stripped of project-induced ties. It adds a new person-centred metric for spotting latent helpers and boundary spanners. Field work over three months in Pomerini, Tanzania, finds that sociotechnical setups, not charismatic hubs, underwrite durable teamwork.
arxiv-2602-20209:
Finding proteins depends on protein matching, and de novo peptide reading from mass spectra is a crucial approach. Existing learning models poorly enforce a basic constraint: a guessed peptide's mass must match the lab-measured precursor mass. A 2026 arXiv paper by Shaorong Chen and two co-authors introduces DiffuNovo, a diffusion model guided by a regressor for de novo peptide sequencing with peptide-level mass control.

Earlier methods often treat mass information as one input feature among others, or use it only in cleanup. That leads to unlikely guesses breaking a physical property. DiffuNovo applies the mass constraint at two key stages. During training, a peptide-level mass loss guides model tuning. At inference, guidance from a guide model, applied through gradient-based updates in latent space, steers output toward mass-consistent peptides. Readers gain a reading model that treats mass match as a constraint, not an extra.
arxiv-2602-20609:
Accurate aerodynamic field prediction matters for vehicle drag evaluation, but high-fidelity fluid dynamics costs too much for iterative design. Zhenhua Zheng and six co-authors note that learning-based methods are fast yet struggle to capture both long-range shape effects and fine local flow structures. Current methods encode shape only once at the input and predict in one shot, diluting global shape awareness and blurs sharp local flow changes. Their network, GA-Field, fixes both gaps.

GA-Field injects a compact 3D shape embedding at many stages to preserve long-range shape consistency, and it refines fields from coarse to fine to recover sharp local details. The network sets state-of-the-art scores on ShapeNet-Car and the large DrivAerNet++ benchmark for surface pressure, wall shear stress, and 3D velocity prediction. It generalizes strongly out of distribution across vehicle categories, a key trait for design work.
arxiv-2602-20709:
Riccardo Gallon and three co-authors tackle straylight faults in space camera sensors, where sunlight near the field of view creates flare. Their AI method segments these flare effects in images, aiming at use aboard spacecraft with tight hardware limits.

The approach stresses broad coverage across diverse flare textures. It uses pre-training on a public data set, Flare7k++, holding flares in varied non-space scenes to offset the scarcity of realistic space data. A DeepLabV3 model with a MobileNetV3 backbone does the segmentation, and the team adds custom metrics tying the model to the onboard navigation pipeline.
arxiv-2602-20809:
Yun-Jui Tsai and four co-authors borrow a human learning trick for AlphaZero-style agents: revisit the positions where you went wrong, rather than always starting fresh. Earlier search-control work sampled past states evenly, ignoring which states held the most learning value.

Their Regret-Guided Search Control adds a regret network that spots high-regret states. These are states where the agent's judgment diverged most from the true outcome. The states go into a priority buffer for reuse as new starting points. Across 9x9 Go, 10x10 Othello, and 11x11 Hex it beats AlphaZero and Go-Exploit by 77 and 89 Elo on average. It also lifts a strong Go model against KataGo from about 69 percent wins to about 78 percent.
arxiv-2602-20909:
Affine frequency division multiplexing is a promising waveform for fast-moving wireless links, but most theory treats signals in discrete time only. Michele Mirabella and four co-authors build a continuous-time framework for it in this 2026 arXiv paper, based on the affine Fourier series. Their analysis shows strictly bandlimited pulses and subcarrier suppression are essential to keep the transmitted signal multicarrier.

The paper derives the power spectral density of AFDM, compares it with other multicarrier schemes under realistic pulse shaping, and tests sensitivity to phase noise, frequency offset, and sampling jitter. Closed-form Cramer-Rao bounds show the chirped modulation raises estimation variance yet resolves Doppler ambiguities. The results lay groundwork for real AFDM transceivers.
arxiv-2602-21109:
A knot can have many ribbon-concordant predecessors, but how many can be fibered? John Baldwin, Jonathan Hanselman, and Steven Sivek answer in this 2026 arXiv paper, removing the hyperbolic restriction from earlier work. They prove every knot in three-space has only finitely many fibered predecessors under ribbon concordance.

The key step is an inequality relating the knot Floer homology of a generalized satellite knot to that of its companion, proved through immersed curves in bordered Heegaard Floer homology. Combined with results of Kojima and McShane, the work also bounds the Gromov norm of any fibered predecessor's complement in terms of the arc index and genus of the original knot.
arxiv-2602-21209:
Ternary Leibniz algebras extend a classical algebraic structure to three inputs. Ahmed Zahari Abdou Damdji classifies the four-dimensional case in this 2026 arXiv paper, up to isomorphism, over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. For each non-abelian algebra in the classification, the centroid and quasi-centroid are determined explicitly with their dimensions.

The results give a comprehensive picture of the internal symmetries of low-dimensional ternary Leibniz algebras. They extend classical results from the binary Leibniz setting into the ternary world. Readers get a complete catalogue for dimension four plus symmetry data for every non-abelian entry.
arxiv-2602-21309:
Black strings in tweaked gravity offer a testing ground for how matter and shape mix. L. C. N. Santos, L. G. Barbosa, and C. C. Barros study exact black string answers in this 2026 arXiv paper, in a gravity theory coupling bend to the trace of the stress-energy tensor. An uneven Kiselev fluid fills the space-time.

Static tube-shaped answers extend to spinning ones by grid switch. The authors map how the quintessence dial and matter-shape coupling shape geometry, and where weak, null, and strong energy rules hold. Tunnel of scalar bits across the horizon yields a Hawking heat, while heat room reveals heat steadiness and phase-shift rules.
arxiv-2602-21509:
Jinwon Park and three co-authors propose Fair Model-based Clustering, a fair clustering algorithm built on a finite mixture model. Fair clustering seeks clusters whose sensitive-attribute shares, such as gender or race, resemble those of the whole dataset. Existing fair methods often modify K-means to satisfy a fairness constraint.

A critical limit of several existing methods is parameter count: because each datum's cluster assignment must be optimized alongside cluster centers, learnable parameters grow with sample size, blocking scale-up. The new method breaks that link. Its parameter count stays independent of sample size, so mini-batch learning can yield approximately fair clusters at scale. It also handles non-metric data like categorical data whenever the likelihood is well-defined. Theory and experiments support its superiority.
arxiv-2602-22209:
First-person videos of people handling objects are brutally hard to reconstruct: hands hide objects, objects leave the frame, and separate estimates of hand and object often disagree. Yufei Ye and three co-authors present WHOLE, a method that rebuilds hand and object motion together in world space from egocentric video, given object templates. Its core is a learned generative prior over hand-object motion.

At test time, the prior is guided to produce trajectories that match what the video shows, reasoning jointly about interaction instead of patching separate estimates. The joint approach substantially beats separate hand-then-object pipelines. WHOLE sets a new state of the art on hand-object benchmarks, offering robots and AR systems a truer picture of manipulation.
arxiv-2602-22609:
Guangyu Hu and three co-authors close a benchmark gap in hardware model checking. Existing suites are few, often ship only as BTOR2 files without the original register-transfer-level designs, and skew toward extremes where cases are trivial or hopeless. That skew warps evaluation and lets solver tuning overfit a narrow set.

EvolveGen pairs reinforcement learning with high-level synthesis to grow fresh benchmarks. An agent learns to build computation graphs, which compile under varied synthesis directives into functionally equal but structurally distinct hardware pairs, yielding hard checking cases. Solver runtime serves as the reward, so the agent finds small-but-hard instances that expose solver weaknesses. Tests show diverse standard-format benchmarks that reveal bottlenecks in leading checkers.
arxiv-2602-22709:
Tanagodchaporn Inyanya and fifteen co-authors report a free-floating planet candidate caught by microlensing. Such planets, cast out from their birth systems, shine too faintly to see directly, but their gravity briefly magnifies a background star. Event KMT-2024-BLG-3237 showed a small, fast brightening: under one magnitude over under three days, with strong finite-source effects.

The Einstein timescale runs about half a day, and the angular Einstein radius measures about six microarcseconds, the eleventh isolated microlens with so small a radius. Mass hinges on unknown relative parallax: roughly Neptune-mass at one parallax value, Saturn-mass at another, with a Bayesian estimate near sixty-seven Earth masses at about seven kiloparsecs. Searches for a host star found no significant evidence.
arxiv-2602-22809:
Mingde Yao and four co-authors let users skip step-by-step photo-editing instructions. Editing quality today hinges on carefully crafted prompts, dumping task breakdown and sequencing on the user. PhotoAgent instead treats autonomous editing as long-horizon decision making.

It reasons over aesthetic intent, plans multi-step edits through tree search, and refines results in a closed loop with memory and visual feedback, needing no per-step prompts. For reliable real-world evaluation, the team built UGC-Edit, a benchmark of 7,000 photos with a learned aesthetic reward model, plus a test set of 1,017 photos. Experiments show PhotoAgent consistently improves both instruction adherence and visual quality over baselines.
arxiv-2602-23109:
Kai Chen and two co-authors make human-robot exchange clear in hidden walker cases through active reasoning. The sudden arrival of hidden walkers is a critical safety challenge in autonomous driving, and usual rule or purely data-led methods struggle with the built-in high doubt of these rare cases. Their framework gives the agent a human-like, belief-led process.

A Rao-Blackwellized Particle Filter fast gauges the walker's mixed state, while a Conditional Belief Reset process and a Hypothesis Injection technique plainly model beliefs about the walker's several hidden aims. Plans come via a Cross-Entropy Method boosted Model Predictive Path Integral controller, which joins the fast, repeat search of CEM with the built-in toughness of MPPI. Sim runs show sharply reduced crash rates against reflex, rule, and reward-led baselines, with clear and human-like driving conduct mirroring the agent's inner belief state.
arxiv-2602-23309:
Cerruti and five co-authors test whether the blazar S5 1044+71 hosts a precessing jet from its supermassive black hole. The bright gamma-ray blazar shows strong quasi-periodic oscillations in Fermi-LAT data, about three years apart. With a new gamma-ray cycle complete, the team revisits the periodicity and analyzes all multi-wavelength data for correlations and time lags.

Data span Fermi-LAT, NuSTAR, Swift, AstroSat, ASAS-SN, ZTF, Pan-STARRS, NEOWISE, plus Palomar and Pulkovo history. The periodicity is confirmed, with significant spectral variability in gamma-ray, X-ray, and optical/UV bands. Low-energy data correlate with gamma-rays at an index near one, X-rays more mildly near three tenths, and no significant time lag appears. A precessing jet model fits the Fermi-LAT light curve. Spectral energy fits place the gamma-ray emission beyond the broad-line region, consistent with a precessing relativistic jet.
arxiv-2602-23409:
Michael Poppel and four co-authors tackle long-range frequency tuning for quantum learning. Angle-encoded variational circuits output a truncated Fourier series, but fixed unary encoding needs about as many encoding gates as the maximum frequency. Trainable-frequency circuits promise relief by learning prefactors beside the ansatz parameters, adapting the spectrum to the target.

The barrier: the prefactor gradient is suppressed by the spectral gap, pinning movement near initialization. Ternary grid initialization sets prefactors to powers of three, so every target frequency lies within half a unit of the spectrum at start. On a synthetic benchmark with shifted target frequencies, ternary initialization reaches median R-squared of zero point nine nine seven versus zero point one eight for unary. All runs beat zero point nine five, against none for unary. Even CMA-ES with twenty times the budget reaches only 25 percent.
arxiv-2602-24109:
Sara Nabhani and three co-authors present ARGUS, a framework for studying how narrative features affect persuasion in argumentative texts. The 2026 paper asks whether stories make arguments more persuasive online, and which narrative features matter most. That question is underexplored for unstructured online argumentation, despite stories' reputation as powerful persuasive tools.

ARGUS introduces a new corpus from the ChangeMyView forum, annotated for story presence and six key narrative features. It joins two theoretical frameworks that capture textual narrative traits and their effects on readers. Using both encoder-based classifiers and zero-shot large language models, the framework identifies stories and narrative features at scale. In short, the team can now count stories at scale. The counts show which story parts sway readers. That influence is the heart of the study. The study tests it online.
arxiv-2603-00009: Mekkaoui and Pham study infinite-horizon Markov decision processes with heterogeneous agents, a continuum of them, interacting through common noise, without assuming exchangeability. Lifting the control problem to a standard Markov decision process on the Wasserstein space of label-state measures proves their strong and label-state formulations equivalent. The value function emerges as the unique fixed point of a Bellman operator there. They also give sharp finite-population bounds for propagation of chaos, yielding near-optimal finite-agent policies from near-optimal limiting policies.
arxiv-2603-00109: Kovalenko presents CASCADE, a system that sharpens coarse geophysical fields by moving detail along learned flow paths instead of inventing pixel detail. It splits motion into large and subgrid parts, mirroring the closure problem in weather prediction, and keeps coarse consistency through an assimilation correction step. Tested on SEVIR radar data at 4x sharpening of severe convective storms, it beats baselines on continuous scores and threshold skill scores. Its visible velocity and correction fields make its workings interpretable, and its outputs stay coherent in time and true to mass conservation.
arxiv-2603-00209: Turan and Munkhammar propose a quantile-based piecewise method for rebuilding densities from data. Classical global moment approximations often oscillate, destabilise in the tails, and hinge on support. Their approach pairs equal-probability binning with local moment polynomials in each bin, in monomial and Lagrange variants. Bin counts and degrees come from a grid search steered by the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test under non-negativity rules. Across benchmarks, the methods cut K-S errors by about 80 to 96 percent against standard approaches, and by about 83 to 97 percent against splines.
arxiv-2603-00309: Yang and colleagues study language-model agents that work together with no preset roles or workflows. In such free-form teamwork, duplicated effort and cascading failures often arise. They introduce the Dynamic Interaction Graph, tracking agent activations and interactions over time as a causal network. The graph makes such teamwork observable and explainable. From teamwork paths alone, it supports live spotting, explanation, and correction of teamwork-caused error patterns. The authors argue this fills a key gap in grasping how general agents solve problems together.
arxiv-2603-00509: Zhang and three colleagues extend COLE, a column based learned store for blockchains, to handle forks and pruning that the original handled poorly. A rewind capable in memory tree with content defined chunking keeps a consistent hash digest per block through chain reorganisations. On disk, a new two level Merkle tree called a prunable version tree enables efficient state pruning. The enhanced COLE design thus keeps the storage and throughput gains of columnar learned indexing while supporting reorganisation and pruning.
arxiv-2603-00709: Pagnier and four colleagues choose among rival system models with a closed loop optimal control method, picking the input that best splits model replies. The approach assumes control over one system input plus readings of its reply, then compares telling replies against observed data to name the best model. Computer runs show the method works before an electrophysiology experiment, where it cleanly splits models of photocurrents from opsin dynamics. The work shows mechanism based modelling can tell models apart interpretably, from simulation through to live experiment.
arxiv-2603-01209: May and five colleagues show agent evaluations hide a runtime trap: agents trained with variable-keeping runtimes collapse when deployed statelessly, where variables clear between actions. In a subset-picking task under a weight limit, a persistent-trained agent at 80 calls per turn scores 61 percent of optimal statelessly versus 77 percent matched. It burns over four times the tokens rebuilding its record. A tighter cap of 25 calls crashes mismatched quality to 7 percent while matched quality holds at 66 percent, so tests must cover runtime transfer and report cost with quality.
arxiv-2603-01309: Steier surveys PAC guarantees for reinforcement learning from 2018 to 2025. The promise: with probability at least 1 minus delta, a learned policy lands epsilon-close to optimal after N episodes. His Coverage-Structure-Objective framework splits nearly every PAC complexity result into coverage, structure, and objective: how data were obtained, intrinsic complexity, and what the learner must deliver. The core covers tight tabular baselines, the uniform-PAC bridge to regret, complexity measures like Bellman rank and Bellman-Eluder dimension, and results for linear, kernel, and low-rank models.
arxiv-2603-01509:
Text-to-video models can make striking clips, but the words you type steer the result more than most users expect. Zillur Rahman, Alex Sheng, and Cristian Meo address that prompt problem in this 2026 work. Fixes that edit the clip later can add flaws, while retraining the core model costs too much for most teams.

Their framework, called 3R, improves the prompt itself and needs no training of the video model. It pulls helpful modifiers from a search base, tunes prompts toward what people prefer, and smooths frames over time. Any current video model can sit behind the same front end. Tests show gains in still-image quality and in smooth motion across a clip, which points to prompt design as a cheap lever.
arxiv-2603-02009:
Marcelo Cavalcanti and Valeria Domingos Cavalcanti settle two questions for a damped quintic wave equation in this 2026 work. The setting is a three-dimensional bounded domain with Kelvin-Voigt damping placed only in part of it. Localized damping steals derivatives, while the critical quintic term pushes solutions hard.

First, they prove well-posedness for arbitrarily large initial data, so solutions exist and behave stably. Frequency-space tools and Bernstein inequalities lift the damping term into a workable framework for Strichartz estimates. Second, they prove the energy decays uniformly at an exponential rate over time. Microlocal defect measures handle the weak residual left by the damping mechanism. A sharp unique continuation result closes the observability argument, even for damping regions of tiny measure.
arxiv-2603-02409:
Kathryn Jones, Brett Morris, and Kevin Heng study how chemistry shapes reflected light from hot Jupiters in this 2026 paper. A geometric albedo measures how much starlight a planet reflects at full phase. Space telescopes have measured albedos across many bands for many planets. The team curates a broad sample and cleans it of thermal glow contamination.

A hierarchical Bayesian model searches for trends with planet traits. Equilibrium temperature, gravity, and host star metal content are all tested. Albedo distributions from different telescopes show no clear statistical split. A first-principles model then tests which gases drive the patterns. Sodium and water emerge as the key absorbers shaping reflection. Adding two metal oxides without condensation wipes albedos out, against the data.
arxiv-2603-03009:
Wenze Chen, Haojie Hou, Ruibo Ma, and Dong Yao compute the odds of a major outbreak exactly at an epidemic's tipping point. Their 2026 paper studies a susceptible-infected process on a network that keeps rewiring: links between healthy and sick nodes break, and healthy nodes reconnect at random. At the critical infection rate, small chances decide whether one case sparks a huge outbreak.

A single quantity built from the degree distribution's first three moments governs the transition's character. When it is positive, the outbreak chance from one initial case follows a precise power law in network size, with an explicit constant the authors derive. When negative, the chance is far smaller still. The split mirrors known behavior in classic random graphs.
arxiv-2603-03209:
Margaret Ridder, Paul Barrett, Craig Heinke, and Gregory Sivakoff search six cataclysmic variable stars for coherent radio emission. These binary systems, where a white dwarf pulls gas from a companion, show wildly varied radio behavior: jet-like flares in some, strongly polarized narrow signals in others. Their 2026 study analyzes two radio bands from the Very Large Array.

The team found both broadband and narrowband emission that is highly polarized and variable, matching electron-cyclotron maser emission or plasma radiation. Narrow bands suggest one isolated emitting region, while broad bands fit a region with varying magnetic field or density. One target varied within minutes with little polarization, possibly from the white dwarf's magnetosphere colliding with blobs of diamagnetic gas. The survey sharpens the menu of emission mechanisms in these systems.
arxiv-2603-03409:
Haipeng Luo offers a short note on the Squint algorithm for the classic expert problem in online learning. In that problem, a learner repeatedly spreads weight across many experts while an adversary sets each expert's loss. Good algorithms keep regret low, meaning they nearly match not just the single best expert but the best small group of experts in hindsight.

Luo describes a simple variant of Squint, an established algorithm for this task. A small change to the original proof shows the variant achieves a regret bound resembling one recently proved for a variant of another known method, NormalHedge. The note is deliberately brief: one modification, one adjusted proof, one clean guarantee. It will interest specialists in online learning theory who track the fine differences between quantile regret bounds.
arxiv-2603-03509:
Justin Shotton and twenty-four colleagues catch one quantum instability strangling another before it forms. In layered metals, a matching Fermi surface shape often triggers a charge density wave, a frozen ripple of charge. The van der Waals material UTe3 shows exactly that nesting shape in photoemission measurements, similar to relatives that do form waves. Yet an extensive search finds no wave in UTe3 at all.

The culprit is the Kondo effect. Uranium's localized electrons hybridize strongly with tellurium states, entangling local moments with roaming electrons. That hybridization rebuilds the low-energy electronic structure and removes the instability, preempting the density wave entirely. The 2026 result is a rare clean case of Kondo physics blocking a competing order, and it suggests a route to controlling ordering in correlated two-dimensional materials.
arxiv-2603-03609:
Ryoya Nakamura and seven others correct how spin currents are measured in layered crystals. Layered substances attract spin research, but their conduction differs wildly by direction, which quietly corrupts standard estimates of spin Hall conduction and spin spreading length. Their 2026 study examines the layered metal PtTe2, combining a finite element model in three dimensions with nonlocal spin valve measurements.

A new theoretical treatment handles uneven spin spreading with the same machinery as the familiar even model. It extracts spreading lengths along both directions, within the layers and across them. The comparison delivers the warning: the conventional isotropic assumption overestimates key values, particularly the out-of-plane spreading length and the spin Hall conduction. Device designers working with layered substances need the uneven-spreading correction, the authors argue.
arxiv-2603-03909: Zisis and Sætrom present an ultrabubble enumeration method for pangenomic variation graphs based on lowest common ancestor queries. Biedged graphs use black edges for sequences and grey edges for adjacencies. Ultrabubbles are acyclic subgraphs representing a set of sequence variants all starting and ending with two distinct sequences, entering and exiting through two black edges. The authors show any bidirected graph transforms into a biedged graph where lowest common ancestor queries decide whether a snarl is an ultrabubble. That yields a faster algorithm than the naive approach.
arxiv-2603-04009: Berger and Oliva present a method of uniform realizability interpretations unifying realizability treatments of logic. Older realizability, such as Kleene number realizability, demands stated witnesses for existential quantifiers, while newer methods treat some quantifiers alike. The new notion abstracts these gaps by tuning interpretation through a given treatment of atomic formulas, for standard and modern variants.
arxiv-2603-04109: Huber and others test full mediation of treatment effects and causal process identifiability. In causal analysis, understanding how a randomly assigned treatment affects an outcome is central. They propose a test of whether a treatment effect operates exclusively through seen mediators, and whether mediator steps can be identified given covariates. If both hold, a conditionally random treatment becomes independent of the outcome given mediators and covariates. They extend the method to non-random treatments, where full mediation stays testable but identification fails, implemented with double machine learning.
arxiv-2603-04209: De Sanctis and others go beyond edge deletion for counterfactual explanation in graph neural networks. Counterfactual explanations, minimal changes flipping a model's output, give a clear window onto network conduct. The authors present XPlore, broadening the counterfactual search space through gradient-guided changes to adjacency and node feature matrices, done together within one gradient-based method. Tests on 13 real-world plus 5 synthetic benchmarks show large validity and fidelity gains over leading rivals while keeping runtime competitive.
arxiv-2603-04309: Kulkarni and colleagues analyze 500 carotid plaques from the multi centre CREST-2 trial for stroke risk markers. Their kernel based additive model combines coherence loss and group sparse regularization for nonlinear classification. Feature group effects appear in partial dependence plots, keeping the model interpretable. The method assesses plaques accurately and links plaque texture strongly to clinical risk. Texture thus emerges as a key signal for judging dangerous plaques.
arxiv-2603-04809: Chowdhury and colleagues present WhisperAlign for long-form Bengali speech hearing and speaker tags. Long-form multi-speaker Bengali audio tests voice spotting, mixed speech, and context memory. A robust chunking plan uses whisper-timed segments fed to a fine-tuned sound model for accurate text. For speaker tags, a joint pipeline uses pyannote.audio and WhisperX. Domain-niche tuning of the Pyannote splitting model on the contest dataset captures Bengali chat nuances. Smart timed chunking plus aimed splitting fine-tuning improves mixed speaker edge fix.
arxiv-2603-04909: Sam Adriaensen and colleagues study hat guessing on graphs where the adversary may only offer proper colorings. They ask for the largest color count under which a neighborhood strategy still guarantees a correct guess. For complete graphs on n vertices they prove the number is 2n minus 1, roughly double the classical value, using perfect matchings between middle layers of the Boolean poset. Every tree on at least 3 vertices has hat guessing number 4, with general upper bounds and exact numbers for graphs up to 4 vertices.
arxiv-2603-05009: Anirban Chatterjee and Yungui Gong test two Gong-Zhang parametrizations, GZ1 and GZ2, against late-time probes: Type Ia supernovae, DESI baryon acoustic swings, cosmic chronometers, and growth-rate data. Bayesian analysis with Akaike and Bayesian information criteria finds both competitive late-time alternatives to ΛCDM, with GZ2 giving tighter constraints and fewer degeneracies. Both recover matter-dominated actions at high redshift with controlled drifts, plus stable accelerated growth. Setup entropy shows the entropy-production rate sensitively capturing dynamical dark energy's influence on late-time structure making.
arxiv-2603-05109: Luigi de Santis and the rest of the team test Boltzmann Generators, generative models sampling balance setups from the Boltzmann spread, where usual runs suffer severe dynamical bottlenecks. Focusing on a Lennard-Jones fluid's liquid-gas key point, they show the generators catch key actions signatures, perform reliably when trained near criticality, and extrapolate across nearby states. The model's leanness metric closely follows underlying phase boundaries, suggesting a link between generative scores and thermodynamics. Small open system sizes remain a limit, suppressing large swings characterizing key phenomena.
arxiv-2603-05409: Jonathan E. Moussa reduces magic state preparation cost with surface-code lattice surgery through recursive 15-to-1 distillation. For a rotated surface code of distance d, T preparation requires a d-by-3d data-qubit grid for up to 15d error correction cycles. CCZ preparation requires a 3d-by-2d grid for up to 10.5d cycles. However, a lower physical error threshold than the underlying surface code's is required.
