It matches the output magic state's error probability with the output surface code's logical error rate at large code distances.
arxiv-2603-05809: Walsh looks at Luo and Lin's new approach to quartic equations, testing it by code and by theory. Using it gives a fully basic, direct route to Bumby's rule, 3X to the fourth minus 2Y squared equals 1. The paper also puts forth a guess that, once settled, would allow similar proofs across a maybe endless family of similar rules.
arxiv-2603-05909: Taranukhin and team propose InfoGatherer, pulling information from papers and follow-up questions. Language models serve high-stakes answers in triage and legal help, yet queries arrive vague and one search pass proves too little. Follow-ups can elicit facts, but methods rely on hidden trust signals, hiding what remains unknown, what matters, and when to stop. InfoGatherer models doubt with Dempster-Shafer beliefs over a proof network, fusing clashing proof without settling too soon. Across legal and medical tasks, it beats baselines in fewer turns, moving toward trusted support.
arxiv-2603-06209: Kukkadapu and his team characterise a joined LVDT sensor and voice coil drive built for seismic isolation in gravitational wave detectors. A set-up with a precision translation stage and balance, plus a finite element simulation method, checks and models an Einstein Telescope pathfinder Type-A unit. Tests and simulation agree well: LVDT response differs by only 1.3 percent from forecast, with high linearity across a plus minus 5 millimetre range. Voice coil force matches simulation within error bars, backing the design for slow suspension control.
arxiv-2603-06309: Abdukhalikov and Verma study quasi-twisted and additive constacyclic codes through a polynomial approach. They describe quasi-twisted codes over finite fields with polynomials, and find the Euclidean, Hermitian, and symplectic duals for index 2 codes. Self-orthogonality rules follow, plus a match between length lm index l quasi-twisted codes over Fq and length m additive constacyclic codes over Fq^l. Additive trace inner products link to quasi-twisted Euclidean and symplectic inner products. The match yields additive trace duals from quasi-twisted Euclidean and symplectic duals.
arxiv-2603-06509: Schmitz tests particle pushers for relativistic trajectories in PIC plasma simulations, where correct integration and error care matter for judging run truth. Many studied systems contain fast particles. Various new schemes for their paths have appeared over recent decades to improve accuracy in specific cases. The article presents a full comparison focused on explicit plans, finding a key class wide to arbitrary high order, plus fourth-order variants against their second-order counterparts.
arxiv-2603-06609: Salem presents a practical feature-level hypothesis testing approach joining the Conditional Shuffle Test with TabPFN, a tabular-data chance foundation model. Modern models are highly rich but difficult to analyze by stats. Black-box guessers rarely give valid tests or p-values for whether single features carry information about a target variable. The final procedure gives finite-sample valid p-values for conditional relevance of inputs, even under nonlinear and linked settings, without new training or set assumptions.
arxiv-2603-06809: Twardowski and colleagues study how front surface coatings affect particle generation when relativistic lasers strike thick high-Z targets. Such lasers produce hot electrons and secondary particles for radiography, cancer therapy, and isochoric heating, and lower-density or structured coatings can improve coupling. At Scarlet, an intense pulse hit coatings on thick tantalum: plastic, foam, and gold nanowire layers. Less absorption tracks smaller post-damage craters, while more absorption yields more MeV electrons and X-rays, with bare targets best for electron and X-ray generation.
arxiv-2603-06909: Sankar and colleagues run a random trial of dispatcher-run contrail avoidance inside normal flight planning, built to scale across an airline network. Contrails drive a large share of flight warming, and steering around them promises relief, yet earlier trials used custom forecast links. Their system was checked with satellite photos and an auto flight-contrail attribution tool. Eligible flights dropped in contrail making against controls, and flights that followed avoidance as planned showed a much larger drop.
arxiv-2603-07109: Luo and colleagues test whether vision-language models truly grasp physical transformation, using ConservationBench. The benchmark spans four conserved properties with paired conserving and non-conserving scenes, yielding 23,040 questions across 112 models. Results show systematic failure near chance level, and gains on conservation tasks come with drops on controls. Neither sharper time resolution, prompting, nor curated sampling helps, and text priors favoring invariance do not rescue visual reasoning.
arxiv-2603-07309: Rodriguez-Martin and colleagues test how 5G delay and jitter disturb time-aware scheduling in a combined 5G and time-sensitive network. Deterministic factory links need bounded delay, but the random timing of 5G breaks the precise slots of the time-aware shaper. On a testbed with real switches and a commercial 5G network, they measure downlink delay and jitter. The fix is careful tuning of transmission window offsets between switches, set from a high percentile of measured delay.
arxiv-2603-07509: Rizoiu and colleagues track opinion splits on the r/Brexit forum with a smooth polarity score replacing discrete stance labels. Future stance prediction turns out confounded by survivorship bias: who stays active reflects engagement, not stance. Echo chambers dominate, with a large share of exchanges occurring between like-minded users. Current scores predict future scores best, with echo-chamber immersion second, showing an entrenched partisan core.
arxiv-2603-07709: Zaraket and Mougenot design YAQIN, a culturally sensitive agentic AI for mental healthcare support among Muslim women in the United Kingdom. Services often lack tools for cultural needs, leaving women feeling their values are pathologized. YAQIN combines a faith-aware chatbot with guided journaling grounded in Islamic psychology and user-centered design. A co-designed study with Muslim women and a mental health expert found it bridges cultural gaps in trust and therapeutic confidence.
arxiv-2603-07809: Gutzeit and colleagues study when the verbose persistent homology transform is not one-to-one, for graphs whose corners are all on one line. Given general setup, the VPHT is one-to-one, meaning shapes can be rebuilt using only the VPHT. They find needed and enough traits for failure to rebuild of such graphs, bringing the field closer to a complete sorting.
arxiv-2603-08009: Narayan shows that the quantum metric serves as a sensitive probe of the persistent spin helix. Such helices are symmetry-protected spin textures arising when spin-orbit coupling strengths balance, backing long-lived spin structures for spintronics and spin control. Within the Rashba-Dresselhaus Hamiltonian, the author evaluates the quantum metric parts. He finds a divergent geometric contribution exactly at the persistent spin helix condition, tracing to a hidden line degeneracy when Rashba and Dresselhaus strengths match. Cubic spin-orbit terms tame the response and control its scaling.
arxiv-2603-08309: Elisha and colleagues present concept-guided fine-tuning to steer Vision Transformers away from spurious correlations and improve robustness. These models often degrade under distribution shifts because they lean on spurious correlations, such as background cues, rather than meaningful features. Existing regularization methods usually rely on foreground-background masks, which miss the fine-grained concepts defining an object, such as a long beak and wings for a bird. The new framework steers model reasoning toward concept-level meaning by aligning internal relevance maps with spatially grounded concept masks.
arxiv-2603-08809: Mingshu Cai and colleagues watermark 3D Gaussian splat scenes with an explainable, representation-native design. A Trio-Experts module picks carrier Gaussians, while a budget-aware gate splits carriers from visual compensators. A channel-wise mask steers gradients to hold fidelity, and decoupled tuning reveals where each message bit lives and why, beating prior methods on quality and bit accuracy.
arxiv-2603-09209: Xupeng Chen builds a stress test for an economy hit by fast AI uptake. The core risk is a mismatch: plentiful AI-made output beside weak demand, since institutions rest on scarce human cognition. He models three channels: a displacement spiral where labor substitution cuts income and demand, a Ghost GDP wedge between measured output and spendable income, and shrinking middleman margins. Conditions on growth, spread, and reinstatement rates mark when feedback settles or turns explosive.
arxiv-2603-09309: Yuyang Dai and Yuxia Wang show that the scale on which language models state their confidence is not a neutral design choice. Across six models and three datasets, stated confidence piles onto just three round numbers for most replies. Varying scale granularity, boundary placement, and range regularity, they find a 0-20 scale improves metacognitive sensitivity over the usual 0-100 format. Boundary compression hurts, and round-number habits persist even on irregular ranges.
arxiv-2603-09409: Nicola Abatangelo proves that balls alone, among open bounded domains, support the mean value formula for polyharmonic functions. The proof adapts Kuran's argument for harmonic functions to the polyharmonic case. A quantitative form of the same rigidity result is also given. So the ball is pinned as the unique shape with this averaging trait, with no other domain able to share it.
arxiv-2603-09509: S. E. Chorfi and colleagues study how to run a viscous Hamilton-Jacobi model backward in time when diffusion degenerates. For the linear parabolic case, Carleman estimates give conditional stability of the backward problem. Linearizing then carries the result to the nonlinear case. With noisy data they use an adjoint-state method for the linear problem and a Van Cittert loop for the other, and tests check both.
arxiv-2603-09809: Muyi Sun and coauthors define a finer audio visual task: naming and outlining exactly which region makes each sound, frame by frame. Past work stayed coarse, asking only whether sound and sight match or where a source sits. They built music and everyday life data sets with masks and text for each frame. Their SSUFormer model tops the new benchmark for both outlining and describing sources.
arxiv-2603-10309: Jiangdong Ai and Mingyu Liu sharpen the Alon-Babai-Suzuki bound for families of sets whose intersections fall in a fixed set L. Their refinement counts what the shadows miss on the top levels, tightening the classic bound rather than restating it. In the modular case they track which binomial terms truly appear in the annihilator polynomial, giving a gap-free bound from active support levels alone. For consecutive residues the bound takes a sharp collapsed form, partly answering a question from Alon, Babai, and Suzuki in the negative.
arxiv-2603-10409: Xujing Wang and co-authors propose Differentiable Geometric Indexing for generative retrieval, where one model both indexes items and searches them. Two conflicts drive the work: discrete indexing blocks gradients, cutting index building off from retrieval goals, and inner product scores inflate popular hub items over long tail ones. Soft teacher forcing with Gumbel-Softmax opens a differentiable path, while shared weights align indexing and decoding spaces. Scaled cosine scores on a unit sphere separate popularity from relevance. Tests on large industry and e-commerce data beat rival baselines.
arxiv-2603-10709: Abdollah Rezagholi and co-authors model early cancer biomarker finding by tiny machines traveling in the bloodstream. Finding cancer early improves outcomes, and chemical cues in the blood could betray it. Simulations mimic the blood vessel setting under varied conditions. Adding features that older models missed, such as non-uniform flow, size-dependent particle mobility, and margination from red blood cell contact, steadily lowered the chances of finding the cues. The smallest vessels still gave the highest chances throughout.
arxiv-2603-10809: Mathilde Leuridan and co-authors introduce a general data hypercube for Earth system data, built on compressed tree structures. Earth datasets now carry rich labels and internal limits that dense cubes handle poorly when the data are uneven, sparse, or branching. Their design describes such spaces accurately and compactly, captures sparsity and links between fields, and stays quick to traverse. Inside the Polytope framework, a system pulls features straight from these cubes, enabling precise pulling of small fields.
arxiv-2603-11309: Alexa Gopaulsingh takes up a question posed by Rosenmann and Ventura: what should independence of two subgroups mean for general groups? Her answer is category-theoretic in flavor. Subgroups are independent when any pair of endomorphisms, one on each subgroup, extends jointly to an endomorphism of the group they generate. She shows almost-disjointness is not enough to force it. She gives necessary and sufficient conditions. She offers a heuristic that settles many cases, while the full answer stays open.
arxiv-2603-11509: Jia and co-authors present Manifold-Optimal Guidance, a new way to steer conditional diffusion models. Classifier-Free Guidance is the standard control, yet high guidance scales cause oversaturation, artifacts, and collapse. The team blames a geometric mismatch: plain guidance pushes samples off the dense data manifold. Their fix recasts guidance as a local optimal control problem with a closed-form Riemannian update. An Auto-MOG schedule also tunes guidance strength on its own, removing manual search. Tests show better fidelity and alignment at almost no extra cost.
arxiv-2603-11709: Wu and co-authors propose a scaling law for educational AI agents, where growth comes from structure, not model size. Classic scaling laws track parameters, data, and compute for language models. For teaching agents, the team names five axes: role clarity, skill depth, tool completeness, runtime capability, and educator expertise. A structured profile spec, AgentProfile, makes those axes concrete and countable. Their platform EduClaw runs on it, with over 330 agent profiles and 1,100 skill modules across K-12 subjects. Richer profiles, they observe, bring predictable performance gains.
arxiv-2603-11909: Pathak and co-authors propose Enformer, a Transformer that forecasts time series with full probability spreads. Standard models lean on fixed likelihood forms or quantile targets, which miss joint patterns across series. Enformer instead learns the spread directly, through a stochastic method called engression with a proper scoring rule. It emits coherent joint paths while keeping the Transformer's grip on long-range links. A space-time sibling, GEnformer, handles data with a space dimension too. On standard benchmarks and epidemic data, both give calibrated forecasts, the authors report.
arxiv-2603-12009: Grimaud, Malyshev, and Moulin forecast how well gamma-ray telescopes could spot axion-like particle dark matter. Such particles may turn into photons inside the magnetic fields of galaxy clusters. That swap would leave absorption-like dips in the spectra of active galactic nuclei behind the clusters. Single pairs vary too much, so the team stacks many nucleus-cluster pairs in mock data. The combined search reaches into a mass range no study has charted yet, and more data should sharpen it further.
arxiv-2603-12109: Zou and co-authors name a failure mode they call information self-locking in trained LLM agents. Outcome-based reinforcement learning can leave agents unable to draw out useful feedback. Worse, they also fail to take in the evidence they do get. Two skills drive the loop: action selection picks what to observe, and belief tracking updates the task picture. Each weak skill starves the other, which dulls the learning signal for both. Their AREW method reweights credit with simple critiques and lifts scores across nine tasks.
arxiv-2603-12509: Kim, Sechayk, Zhou, and Igarashi study how user comments support learning tasks from videos. Videos show whole processes but can omit tacit details and context that learners need. Viewers turn to comment sections for extra guidance and for help adapting steps to their own situations. The team interviewed fourteen users and ran co-watching sessions with eight more. Comments prove critical for learning yet stay poorly integrated at every stage of the process. The authors outline design chances to weave comments into video-based task learning.
arxiv-2603-12609: Daniel Jeans examines how well tau lepton pairs at a Higgs factory collider can support quantum tomography. Spin links between the taus carry signs of entanglement, but they need full event reconstruction. His method uses particle momenta and impact parameters to rebuild each event. It yields several weighted solutions per event, from which spin directions can be drawn. Tests in ideal and realistic detectors show photon angular resolution matters most. Energy resolution and vertex performance matter far less.
arxiv-2603-12909: Alfonso Artigue and co-authors exhibit new classes of surface diffeomorphisms with a C1-generic twist on expansiveness. They find a local residual set of maps that are continuum-wise expansive but not expansive. The two notions, often linked, thus come apart for typical maps in this local sense. They also find an open and dense set where expansiveness does imply being Anosov. That second result ties a weak chaotic trait to a strong, rigid one on surfaces.
arxiv-2603-13009: Angela Carollo and co-authors introduce TwoTimeScales, an R package for hazards that vary over two time scales at once. Event data often carry two clocks, yet software for joint models is scarce. The package fits smooth two-dimensional baseline hazards with P-splines. Proportional hazards and competing risks models are both covered. A breast cancer follow-up dataset shows the fitting and plotting tools in action. The package aims to make two-scale analysis routine in applied work.
arxiv-2603-13209: Amit Anand, with Anne-Catherine de la Hamette, Robert Mann, and Shohini Ghose, studies superposed quantum evolutions. They ask what happens when a regular evolution is mixed with a chaotic one. A Mach-Zehnder interferometer and post-selection let them build and test such superpositions. The quantum kicked top serves as the test system, since its classical motion ranges from regular to chaotic. When the chaotic branch dominates, subsystem entropy can exceed that of the classical mixture. Phase space structure strongly shapes how much entropy is produced.
arxiv-2603-13409: Leonardo Toffolin summarizes the ATLAS Trigger System at the CERN Large Hadron Collider. The trigger cuts the event rate from 40 MHz of bunch crossings to a flow fit for storage and analysis. Run-3, from 2022 to 2026, brought major upgrades to both trigger levels. The hardware-based Level-1 trigger and the software-based High Level Trigger had to cope with higher luminosity and pile-up. Toffolin reviews the main features of the system and its Run-3 performance. The trigger enables precision measurements and new physics searches, he notes.
arxiv-2603-13509: Hongchao Zhang and co-authors extend control barrier functions to differential-algebraic systems. Such systems arise in power networks, chemical processes, and multibody systems, where algebraic constraints encode conservation laws. Standard barrier functions can conflict with the constraint manifold, so they do not apply directly. Their DAE-aware barrier functions use projected vector fields to respect the algebraic structure. They derive conditions for forward invariance of safe sets and extend the framework to higher-index systems. Verification uses sum-of-squares certificates or satisfiability checks.
arxiv-2603-13609: Mohammad Sahnoon, Merkebe Getachew Demissie, and Roberto Souza build a grid-based framework for e-scooter demand prediction in Austin, Texas. Temporal input design for deep learning is often chosen heuristically, though past demand strongly shapes results. Their pipeline converts trip records into hourly pickup and dropoff demand images on a spatial grid. A correlation- and error-based procedure then picks informative historical inputs for the model. Ablation with a baseline UNET model and paired tests set the optimal temporal depth.
arxiv-2603-13709: Bo Ma, Jinsong Wu, and Wei Qi Yan propose REAEDP, a differentially private data release framework with formal guarantees. Data release faces output-side attacks, such as membership inference, attribute inference, and record linkage. REAEDP joins entropy-calibrated histogram release, a synthetic-data mechanism, and attack-based evaluation. They bound how much Shannon entropy can change between adjacent histogram datasets, with an extension to Rényi entropy. That bound lets noise be calibrated for private release. On public datasets, attacks fell toward random-guess levels.
arxiv-2603-13909: AbouNassar, Elshall, and Abdulah propose FedPBS, a federated learning method built for uneven, non-identical client data. It adapts batch sizes to each client's resources, so participation stays balanced. Small-batch clients also get a proximal correction that keeps local updates near the global model. The method blends ideas from FedBS and FedProx. On CIFAR-10 and UCI-HAR under strong data skew, FedPBS beats FedBS, FedGA, MOON, and FedProx, with smooth, stable loss curves.
arxiv-2603-14309: Medic and Nan tackle 3D wheat head segmentation in field laser scans without any hand labels. Manual labeling of cluttered plant point clouds is slow and often infeasible. Their two-stage pipeline starts by projecting the cloud into many 2D views. A zero-shot Grounded SAM pass marks wheat heads in those views, and multi-view fusion builds first 3D guesses. Those noisy labels then train a proper 3D segmentation network. Results beat Wheat3DGS, a recent rival that also skips manual labels.
arxiv-2603-14609: Ferrod and co-authors ground a spatial reasoning dataset in cadastral vector records. Earth observation models still falter at fine spatial questions. GroundSet ties aerial images to checkable land registry data. The set holds 3.8 million labeled objects in 510,000 high-resolution images. Labels span 135 fine semantic classes. Seven spatial reasoning tasks form the test bench. A standard LLaVA model sets the baseline. Strong supervision lets plain models master fine grounding, they show, while zero-shot rivals lag.
arxiv-2603-14809: Huang and co-authors unify coordinate and kinematic calibration for dual-arm robots in one Lie-algebraic frame. Vision-guided arm pairs need tight calibration to work together. Past methods solve transforms well but treat kinematic error as noise. Split error models let small errors stack up. A single product-of-exponentials error model holds all coupled parameters as twists. No artificial error split enters the design. A closed-form Jacobian from Lie derivatives drives joint fitting. Rank checks show the joint problem is well-posed under mild conditions.
arxiv-2603-15509: Egyenes and co-authors test how pulse length changes current-driven oxygen migration in the superconductor YBCO. Short pulses move oxygen atoms in the copper-oxygen chains, which tunes carrier levels or builds memristive devices. Past work used pulses of a millisecond or more, where heat effects blur the picture. Sweeping from 200 nanoseconds to one millisecond, they find the onset current climbs fast below about ten microseconds. Temperature estimates show shorter pulses run cooler, so the process grows more athermal. The finding matters for memristor design.
arxiv-2603-15809: Abedini and co-authors model how one stubborn agent can hijack a multi-agent system. Malicious agents can spread false claims through team chat channels. The team borrows the Friedkin-Johnsen opinion model from social science. The model matches real multi-agent behavior across many test setups. One stubborn, persuasive agent can trigger a takeover cascade. Three classic defenses work but carry costs or slow consensus. Their trust-adaptive defense tunes trust between agents on the fly. Tests show it blocks manipulation while keeping teamwork intact.
arxiv-2603-16109: Matsuda builds modular forms on a level-five theta group. Theta groups gain higher-level kin in this paper series. Part two treats the group of level 5 in depth. Modular forms on that group are built from scratch. Their multiplier systems come out of the construction. A transformation formula for theta functions drives the work. Characteristics on the theta functions shape the final rules. The series widens the classic theta group toolkit.
arxiv-2603-16309: The Omnilingual MT Team presents the first translation system covering over 1,600 languages. Most systems reach about 200 target languages, out of some 7,000 worldwide. Their data plan merges large public corpora with new curated bitext. Two designs specialize a large language model for translation. One is decoder-only, the other encoder-decoder. Models of 1B to 8B parameters matched or beat a 70B baseline. Gains were strongest for languages that baselines could read but not write.
arxiv-2603-16509: Dziarmaga simulates quantum annealing in a 3D random Ising model. He uses a tensor network state, the projected entangled-pair state. The drive crosses from a paramagnetic phase to a spin-glass phase. For an endless lattice, final energy comes from a deterministic method. For a finite lattice, he samples by Monte Carlo. Both setups approach the Kibble-Zurek power law for leftover energy. The match improves as annealing time grows.
arxiv-2603-16909: Ivas and co-authors build a classifier from networks of coupled chaotic oscillators. Scaling such ensembles is costly, and training can fail to converge. Their design reads input as a local resonance, or echo, inside the oscillator group. Coupling terms are not hand crafted. A neural network learns them, matched to the input feature distribution. Tests on synthetic data show the system can classify, recognize patterns, and identify dynamic systems. The team varies oscillator types and layouts to show the approach is general.
arxiv-2603-17009: Vieira and a large team report a search for a light counterpart to a subsolar mass gravitational wave candidate, S251112cm. The event likely involves at least one object lighter than the Sun. Such mergers sit outside the usual neutron star story, so any light counterpart is speculative. The team built a framework that vets and scores candidate transients from many telescopes. They checked 456 candidates, including 67 from the Rubin Observatory. They found no likely counterpart. They argue the framework still sharpens strategy for the next such event.
arxiv-2603-17109: Murhekar and co-authors present SENSE, a lightweight system that turns EEG signals into text while keeping neural data private. Most brain to text systems fine tune large models on raw signals, which is costly and exposes sensitive data. SENSE splits the work in two. On device retrieval maps EEG to a small bag of words. An off the shelf language model then writes text from those words alone. The EEG module has 6 million parameters and runs on device. On a 128 channel dataset, SENSE matched fine tuned baselines.
arxiv-2603-17609: Pinto and co-authors take a high-resolution X-ray look at the black hole candidate MAXI J1810-222. Low-resolution spectra had hinted at a fast wind tied to an absorption feature near 1 keV. XMM-Newton's RGS detector resolves the lines ten times more sharply. The data back a mildly relativistic wind with broad lines, they report. Extra hot gas points to a layered outflow. Magnetic driving looks likely, with heat still helping lift mass.
arxiv-2603-17709: Kulikovsky models impedance in the cathode catalyst layer of a PEM fuel cell. His non-isothermal model treats heat and current together in one frame. Shaking both inputs in phase lowers the layer impedance, he finds. The static polarization resistivity drops with it. The cause is reduced proton transport loss inside the layer. With tuned amplitudes, those losses can vanish in full, he reports. The effect suggests a cheap route to better cell output.
arxiv-2603-17909: Mikytiv, Toninho, and Ferreira present ACTORCHESTRA, a runtime verification tool for Erlang actor systems. Checks must span many actors whose messages cross in random order. Their framework injects code into OTP-style systems to track causal links on its own. A companion language, WALTZ, turns multi-actor properties into live monitors. Three case studies caught tangled behavioral faults in real systems, they report. Overhead tests weigh the safety gain against run cost.
arxiv-2603-18109: Arron reports a bimodal drift rate structure in bursts from the repeating fast radio burst FRB 20240114A. UMAP and HDBSCAN clustering ran on 233 upward-drifting clusters from FAST data. One group of 45 clusters drifts 2.5 times faster than the rest, near 245.6 versus 98.1 MHz per ms. Mixture models back the split, which holds for single-component clusters alone. The split hints at two separate emission regions in the magnetosphere.
arxiv-2603-18309: Hisham and co-authors put a super-resolution net inside MRI rebuild loops for 3D LGE scans. Thin wall parts of the atrium must be found from sparse k-space data. Their hybrid swaps a deep super-resolution net in as the prior step of each loop round. Training runs end to end on preclinical scans thinned after the fact. At all speed-up rates, scores beat three baselines, and left atrium outlines came out more true.
arxiv-2603-18509: Joshi and Mishra study scrambling delay in SYK wormhole teleportation under a gravitational-wave-inspired drive. A periodic Floquet deformation from the SYK4 sector probes the teleportation channel by exact time evolution. Re-optimizing under the drive separates real effects from calibration mismatch. Two amplitude regimes split near epsilon of order J, and the response acts as a low-pass filter. An inspiral chirp delays the fidelity peak by 0.11 per J, confirmed by OTOC measures.
arxiv-2603-18709: Carmeli, Lutz, and Przybyłko ask when conjunctive queries under TGD rules can be answered in linear time. They cover single tests, all tests, counting, direct access, and enumeration. Their approach lifts known yes-no splits from the unconstrained case to two rule classes. One class needs non-recursive rules with small heads or few frontier variables. The other is frontier-guarded full rules. The lift works for all modes except enumeration. Extra examples show why enumeration and looser rule classes stay hard.
arxiv-2603-18809: Taga and Nakao rebuild Watanabe-Strogatz invariants for coupled phase oscillators from operator theory. Systems of N globally coupled oscillators hold N minus 3 conserved quantities. Such invariants shape how synchronization unfolds. The authors link the Liouvillian and Koopman views of the dynamics. A simple product rule for functions under both operators yields explicit invariant candidates. Ratios of those functions give the full invariant set. The method checks out on Ermentrout-Kopell and Kuramoto models, including a higher-order variant. It offers a spectral route to the same classic result.
arxiv-2603-19109: Terol and co-authors search X-ray data for a line that dark matter decay in a nearby galaxy halo would leave. Two candidate particles could emit such a line. They scan survey data from the Large Magellanic Cloud across a wide energy band. No line shows up in the search. That null result sets lower bounds on the dark matter lifetime. It also caps the mixing of sterile neutrinos and the light coupling of axion-like particles. The caps are the strongest yet for masses below five kilo-electronvolts.
arxiv-2603-19609: Peng and co-authors present LoD-Loc v3, a method for aerial localization in dense cities. It aligns building silhouettes with low-detail city models to find the camera pose. The prior version generalised poorly and failed among dense towers. A new synthetic pipeline built InsLoD-Loc, with 100,000 aerial images and instance labels. The method also shifts from semantic to instance silhouette alignment. That shift cuts pose ambiguity in crowded scenes. Tests beat prior methods by a large margin in cross-scene and dense settings.
arxiv-2603-19809: Ding and co-authors test whether generative recommendation really generalizes better than ID-based models. That edge is often claimed but rarely checked in a careful way. They sort each test case by the skill it demands. Some cases need memorization of seen transitions. Others need composing known patterns into unseen ones. Generative models won on the generalization cases. ID-based models won where memorization mattered more. A token-level view showed much generative success is token memorization. A simple indicator that mixes both models improved overall results.
arxiv-2603-20009: Kuffo, Hepkema, and Boncz present SuperKMeans, a fast k-means variant for indexing vector embeddings. Clustering huge embedding sets is a bottleneck for similarity search. It skips dimensions that play no role in matching a vector to its centroid. This trims both data access and compute cost. It clusters up to seven times faster than FAISS and Scikit-Learn on CPUs. It also beats the GPU tool cuVS by up to four times. A recall-based early stop ends runs once centroid quality stalls, saving more time.
arxiv-2603-20409: Martínez and co-authors revisit how gamma rays from dark matter travel toward Earth. WIMP annihilation sparks cascades that end partly in gamma rays. Standard models count losses from pair production on background light. They often ignore the electrons and positrons those losses create. Those particles can scatter light and regenerate high-energy gamma rays. For distant sources, the fuller treatment changes predicted fluxes sharply. Heavy WIMP fluxes shifted by up to a thousandfold in some channels. Current dark matter limits may shift with the WIMP mass assumed.
arxiv-2603-20509: Jeon and co-authors present a unified study of camera-trap species recognition over time. Camera traps power large-scale biodiversity monitoring worldwide. Most research treats the challenge as cross-domain generalization. Practitioners instead need stable accuracy at one fixed site over time. Their benchmark covers 546 traps with a chronological streaming protocol. Biological foundation models underperformed at many sites from the start. Naive adaptation on past data sometimes fell below zero-shot results. Severe class imbalance and temporal shift drive much of the difficulty.
arxiv-2603-20609: Kuang and co-authors study market segmentation when shoppers can switch segments. New data rules make segment choice part of the game. A monopolist then sets a price for each segment. They call a split strategy proof when no group of shoppers gains by moving. In every such split, producer profit stays at the plain monopoly level. Shopper gains range from that level up to the best case for buyers. They build splits that reach each outcome in between.
arxiv-2603-20709: Singh and co-authors grow single crystals of the semimetal LaNiSb3 and probe their transport traits. Crystals grew by the tin flux method. The structure is orthorhombic, in the Pbcm space group. Resistivity stayed metallic from 3 to 300 kelvin. Magnetoresistance was positive and direction dependent, peaking near 8 percent. Its field shape crossed from quadratic to near linear. Hall data show electrons dominate when warm, with holes joining when cold. A two band model fits this mixed carrier picture.
arxiv-2603-20809: Lacasa-Cazcarra studies Spain's 22 percent minimum wage rise of 2019 and its effect on young workers. He uses census grade tax records for the full formal workforce. Several treatment intensity measures ground the design, including two structural bite indicators. Difference in differences and event study estimates agree on the verdict. The reform caused no net job loss for young workers. Elasticities were small, often positive, and intervals include zero with ease. A tourism based test pins the 2020 collapse on COVID, not the wage hike.
arxiv-2603-21009: Silva and co-authors study what point-group symmetry filtering costs in unitary coupled-cluster ansätze. For groups with degenerate representations, the variational cost was unsettled. They prove the symmetry adapted part of amplitude space is a critical subvariety of the energy. So a search with exact gradients cannot tell filtered from unfiltered ansätze at the start. Across six molecules and two basis sets, the full group filter changes energies by a tiny amount. Parameter counts drop sharply, for example in ammonia and methane.
arxiv-2603-21609: Karapanos and Gouveia reflect on what engagement means in digital behavior change interventions. They contrast three projects from the second author's doctoral work, each built to shift everyday behavior. For each project, they lay out why engagement was sought and what effects it was assumed to have. They also compare how engagement was measured and what the key insights were. Finally, they review the strategies each project used to raise engagement. The piece is a reflective comparison meant to sharpen design thinking, not a new trial.
arxiv-2603-22609: Selin, Unéus, and Knudsen study self-tracking by neurodivergent people, with a focus on masking. Masking means hiding traits to fit social norms. The authors ran a workshop with six autistic or ADHD participants who drew their masking experiences. Three then designed personal tracking tools and used them for two weeks to support unmasking. Based on the activities and interviews, tracking placed heavy sense-making and emotional demands on users. Sharing experiences with peers helped validate feelings. The authors offer a working model with three emotional dimensions.
arxiv-2603-22909: Mehlhorn and Nobahari revisit Gabow's fast algorithm for maximum cardinality matching. The algorithm builds many edge-disjoint shortest augmenting paths in each round. A square-root number of rounds suffices. Each round has three parts: find the path length, build a helper graph, and lift paths back. The authors give a new method for the first part. Gabow's version came from Edmonds' primal-dual method for weighted matching. Their route is more direct and easier to teach, they argue. A full implementation is available online.
arxiv-2603-23209: Jeong and six co-authors ask how massive a burst of the first stars can grow. They run cosmological radiation-hydrodynamic zoom-in simulations of small galaxies near redshift 7 to 8. They vary the Lyman-Werner background light and set star formation to peak efficiency. Strong background light delays star birth, then triggers an intense Population III burst. Still, the burst mass stays below a million solar masses. The reason is fast metal pollution from the first supernovae inside each galaxy.
arxiv-2603-23409: Kalweit and three co-authors explore near-optimal carbon strategies for a climate-neutral Europe. Most studies report one cheapest plan and skip close alternatives. The team extends the PyPSA-Eur model with afforestation, biochar, rock weathering, and perennial crops. A generate-alternatives method maps plans that cost up to 5% more. Many mixes of capture, use, transport, and removal reach net zero at small extra cost. A 5% rise covers extremes from zero to full use of each removal option. Extra removal shows no clear cost edge over synthetic fuels.
arxiv-2603-23509: Wu and nine co-authors name a failure mode they call Internal Safety Collapse. In it, a frontier model pours out harmful text while doing a job that looks benign. Their TVD frame builds tasks where harmful output is the only valid finish. The bench holds 53 scenarios across eight professions. On three test cases, worst-case failure rates average about 95 percent across four frontier models. Newer models fail more than older ones, not less. The team warns that skill itself widens the attack surface.
arxiv-2603-23609: Mukherjee and Hansen build a formalism for four-particle effects in lattice decay studies. Four-body states block reads of scattering and decay strengths from lattice runs. Their method links finite box energies and matrix elements to the couplings of the theory. It holds at leading order in pair, quartet, and mixing couplings. A quantization rule then gives box energies up to the six-particle line. The levels show pair-like and quartet-like states trading places. It helps price four-body shares in hadron decays.
arxiv-2603-23709: Cid and Veloso study the isotropy groups of locally finite derivations on a two-variable polynomial ring. They lean on Van den Essen's sorting of such derivations. For each derivation, they compare its isotropy group with that of its linked exponential map. The two groups match when the derivation is locally nilpotent. They may part ways once a semisimple part enters. The pair also prove every nonzero such derivation has a nontrivial isotropy group.
arxiv-2603-23909: Hua and co-authors present DUPLEX, a dual-system planner that keeps language models away from direct planning. Language models can hallucinate and break logic on long tasks. In DUPLEX, a fast system uses a small model only to extract entities and relations from text. Those facts become a PDDL file for a classical planner. If planning fails, a slow system uses solver diagnostics and a larger model to repair the input. Tests across 12 domains beat end-to-end and hybrid baselines, they report.
arxiv-2603-25209: Tian and co-authors stretch short-clip video models to long films without any retraining. Quality drops on long runs for two reasons: frame positions and context length both leave the trained range. FreeLOC fixes each flaw. One step re-encodes time positions at several scales so they feel familiar to the model. Sparse attention then keeps local detail plus far links across time. A probe checks each layer's sensitivity, so fixes land only where needed. Tests beat other no-training methods on steadiness and looks.
arxiv-2603-25609: Balcerzak and Popławski extend theorems of Boros and Menzer on functional equations. One result concerns the equation f of x times f of y equals zero for generalized polynomials. Another covers the matching inequality for generalized monomials of even degree. The authors use methods close to the original proofs. Their change is in how large the Borel plane set D must be. They measure largeness in a mixed sense that joins measure and Baire category.
arxiv-2603-26209: Lemm and Rubiliani review Lieb-Robinson bounds for Bose-Hubbard Hamiltonians and give a shorter proof. These bounds limit how fast signals can spread in a quantum lattice system. Recent work showed the velocity grows at most like t to the power d minus one for large times. Here d is the lattice dimension and the states have bounded density. The authors prove a slightly weaker bound, t to the power d plus epsilon. Their proof is simplified compared with the original argument.
arxiv-2603-26909: Jiang and co-authors explore how blind and low vision people experience urban and public art. Most access research covers museums, while urban work centers on navigation. The team interviewed 16 blind and low vision participants using design probes with AI descriptions. Participants valued spontaneous discovery and touch, sound, and smell engagement. Safety came before art in street settings, though. Inaccurate AI descriptions also risked cultural erasure. The authors derive seven design dimensions for public art access tools.
arxiv-2603-27009: Banerjee and co-authors built interactive software for visualizing higher-order structures in Hilbert geometry. Higher-order Voronoi diagrams and Delaunay mosaics in polygonal metrics lacked any viewing tools. Their tool shows these diagrams together with clustering views. It also explores overlap and outer regions in the Hilbert polygonal metric. The team proves kth-order Voronoi cells are not always star-shaped. They bound the complexity of an algorithm that draws all orders at once. The software extends earlier tools for the Hilbert, Funk, and Thompson geometries.
arxiv-2603-27209: Zhou and co-authors present LightMover, a generative tool for moving and recoloring light in a single photo. The method leans on video diffusion priors to keep illumination changes physically plausible. Light editing becomes a token sequence prediction task over the image. Control tokens set the light's position, color, and intensity together. Reflections, shadows, and falloff adjust along with the light itself. An adaptive pruning scheme cuts the control sequence length by 41 percent. A rendering pipeline generated consistent training pairs across many light settings.
arxiv-2603-27509: Caja-Lopez proves uniqueness for bounded solutions of fuzzy Landau equations. The work also covers the multiespecies Landau system. Proof rests on stability bounds in Wasserstein distance. Those bounds span a wider class of hard equations. The class includes 2D Euler flow and Vlasov-Poisson. Past uniqueness results fall out as special cases. One route adapts a stochastic coupling method. A second route uses a symmetrization trick. Both give matching stability bounds.
arxiv-2603-27609: Behajaina and co-authors study monodromy groups of two-step polynomial maps. Each step is an indecomposable polynomial on its own. The combined group tends to show a largeness trait. Cases that fail fall on an explicit exception list. Such results matter for chains of three or more steps. They also feed problems in arithmetic dynamics. The main theorem is a key part of a companion work. That work solves a long-open Davenport-Lewis-Schinzel problem.
arxiv-2603-27709: Igusa and Maresca chart wall-and-chamber maps for general torsion classes. Torsion classes need not be functorially finite here. Chambers are the connected gaps between walls. Each chamber yields pseudo-torsion and pseudo-torsionfree classes. Those two classes pin down the chamber itself. When both are finitely generated, the chamber is open. Green paths in stability space add stratifications. The work hunts ghost modules left outside the class.
arxiv-2603-27809: Popescu-Belis reflects on what chatbots teach us about human language. Each NLP era is set beside language science views. Rule, statistical, and neural phases all get reviewed. Similarities and gaps with human capacity are drawn out. Modern chatbots show striking language skill. Yet their rise has not deepened our grasp of minds. The essay argues the two fields inform each other weakly. Core questions about human language stay open.
arxiv-2603-28209: Della Torre and three co-authors test whether diffusion-based room impulse response estimates help real microphone array work. A room's impulse response shapes how speech and spatial audio systems perform. Their earlier inpainting method fills in missing responses between measured spots. Here they plug those estimates into practical multi-microphone tasks and check the gains. The method also holds up on real-world recordings, not just simulations. That supports its use in deployed audio systems.
arxiv-2603-28309: Lassoued and five co-authors build a compact transformer that hunts security flaws in C code. Giant language models detect flaws well but cost too much for constant use in coding workflows. Their VulnScout-C has 693 million parameters, with only 353 million active per run. They also release a verified dataset of 33,565 samples that covers rare weakness types. On a standard benchmark, the small model beat all rivals, including big reasoning models and commercial scanners.
arxiv-2603-28509: Kuchař and Macek design lab tests for excited-state quantum phase transitions using a single trapped ion. Such transitions mark sharp changes in highly excited states, not just the ground state. In an extended Rabi model, one family of states sits between two critical energies in its superradiant phase. The authors define witness observables for these states and track their scaling. They map the model's knobs onto Paul trap settings and simulate drives at varied speeds.
arxiv-2603-28709: Azhar and co-authors describe the physical design of UET-RVMCU, a streamlined open-source RISC-V microcontroller. The chip derives from the UETRV-PCore processor. The team cut pipeline stages and removed the memory management unit. They also integrated GPIO peripherals for embedded use. The final GDSII layout came from OpenLane, an open-source RTL-to-GDS flow. The project shows that an application-class system on chip can become a feature-rich microcontroller. The design stresses low area, simplicity, and open-source development.
arxiv-2603-29009: Georgiou, Tang, and Qi present MEDiC, a framework that distills CLIP knowledge into masked image modeling through three objectives. Past methods work in pixel space or in latent feature space alone. MEDiC joins patch level token distillation, global CLS alignment, and pixel reconstruction in one pipeline. All three objectives add complementary information, reaching 73.9 percent kNN accuracy on ImageNet-1K. A new masking scheme made more coherent masks but did not beat simple block masking in this setting. Loss weights proved fragile: small changes cost up to 17 points of accuracy.
arxiv-2603-29109: Yang and co-authors present SemLoc, a tool that finds the faulty lines behind software failures. Standard tools rank code by execution patterns. Those signals fail on semantic bugs, where runs follow the same path. Language model tools reason about meaning but give unverifiable answers. SemLoc turns that free-form reasoning into a typed, checkable form. It builds a matrix of broken constraints across tests. On 250 Python programs, SemLoc reached 42.8 percent top-one accuracy.
arxiv-2603-29909: Le Floch settles a 135-year-old puzzle about 990 quasigroup equation laws. Schröder listed these laws while attacking a claim by Peirce on lattices. Each law equates two three-variable expressions built from quasigroup operations. A quasigroup is a non-associative cousin of a group, with two division operations. He finds all 114 equivalence classes among joined versions of the laws. He also maps every implication between them. Schröder's five-element non-distributive lattice sits inside as a small corner.
arxiv-2603-30009: Acharya constructs additively graceful signed graphs from a starting graph G. The input graph may itself be additively graceful, or it may not. Her method builds new signed graphs that carry the graceful property either way. She also shows how to build fresh examples from signed graphs already known to be graceful. A second thread pins down the values of m and n for which the non-divisible sum graph G(m, n) admits an additively graceful labeling.
arxiv-2604-00009: Aditto presents the design, build attempt, and failure analysis of Eyla, an identity architecture. Unlike methods tuning models for helpfulness, Eyla targets identity consistency under adversarial pressure. Aditto proposes the Identity Consistency Score, a benchmark for testing this property across models. He then gives an account of building it using AI coding helpers as a non-coder. The attempt cost over 1,000 dollars and produced a 1.27B parameter model whose 86 subsystems added under 2 percent to output. His analysis identifies five failure modes of AI-assisted development and offers advice.
arxiv-2604-00209: Wang, Xiong, and Shu ask whether large language models internally encode contextual privacy norms, and why leaks persist when they do. Probing several models, they find the three norm-setting integrity parameters, information type, recipient, and transmission principle, sitting in activation space as distinct directions a linear probe can pull apart. Models still disclose private information in practice, showing a gap between concept representation and behavior. The authors introduce CI-parametric steering along each dimension, which cuts violations better and more predictably than one-size-fits-all steering.
arxiv-2604-00409: Zhou and colleagues demonstrate a strong light response from graphene Josephson junctions at terahertz frequencies, a first step toward graphene-based quantum sensors in that band. Graphene absorbs evenly across frequencies and heats quickly under radiation, which suppresses the junctions' critical current, but earlier work stayed in microwave and infrared ranges where rival detectors already exist. The terahertz band lacks any mature quantum sensor, and the team's low-intensity results point the way there.
arxiv-2604-00609: Jin and colleagues propose TALENT, a tuning framework for referring image segmentation, the task of cutting out a target named in a text phrase. Efficient tuning looks hopeful, yet current methods let visual features light up the named target weakly while also waking unrelated objects of the same category. The authors name this flaw non-target activation and measure it. TALENT fixes it with two parts: a rectified cost aggregator that gathers text-referred features well, and a target-aware learning mechanism that turns stray activation into accurate target activation.
arxiv-2604-00709: Spears and colleagues test electronic friction models, isotropic and anisotropic, for laser-driven hydrogen release on copper's (111) facet, using a ML setup. Fast light-driven changes turn on energy moving from excited electrons to vibrations. When that nonadiabatic transfer is anisotropic, it can steer motion, affecting reaction odds and non-thermal energy spreads. Uneven friction sets how fast energy enters the surface layer and how release odds vary with fluence. Final forward, shaking, and spinning energy spreads follow the energy landscape at the barrier, unmoved by friction details.
arxiv-2604-00809: Zaher, Buisson, and Joly revisit human-in-the-loop object retrieval. A system hunts images of a wanted object class from one user query plus relevance feedback, with no prior labels. They recast the task as binary classification driven by active learning, which picks the most informative samples for annotation at each round. Comparing representation strategies on multi-object data sets, they weigh global context against fine-grained local detail for practical interactive pipelines.
arxiv-2604-00909: Sugiura and team present JAMMEval, a refined set of Japanese benchmarks for sound vision-language model testing. Japanese visual question benchmarks suffer unclear questions, wrong answers, and items solvable without visual grounding, skewing model rankings. JAMMEval refines seven older data sets through two rounds of human review. Its scores better reflect skill, vary less run to run, and tell apart models of varied skill levels more clearly.
arxiv-2604-01209: Bella and colleagues prove regularity theorems in the style of Avellaneda-Lin for random elliptic operators on domains. Interior results of this kind have existed for a while, but on general smooth domains prior theory was largely limited to Lipschitz estimates. The paper establishes C1-alpha regularity on bounded sufficiently smooth domains, and also for scalar problems on convex polytopes. It adds helper results used when deriving fluctuation limits, including a weighted Meyers bound.
arxiv-2604-01309: The Euclid Collaboration tests whether the usual Gaussian assumption holds for inferring cosmological parameters from Euclid's two-point statistics. They model the likelihood with an Edgeworth expansion built from the full skewness tensor. Only the diagonal part matters: adding the whole tensor injects noise without improving accuracy, and limits shift by under 5 percent either way. Tests on 10000 cloned Euclid mocks show no detectable extra skewness at intermediate scales given expected shot noise, so the Gaussian likelihood looks robust in both Fourier and configuration space.
arxiv-2604-01609: Qi and colleagues propose Swift-SVD, a compression method with proven optimum, real speed, and number stability. Swift-SVD pools spread of outputs over a batch of inputs, then performs an eigen split, for training-free, fast, optimal layer-wise low-rank fit. They use effective rank to analyze local squeeze and design dynamic rank sharing jointly weighing local rebuild loss and end-to-end layer weight. Across six language models and eight datasets, Swift-SVD beats state-of-the-art rivals, achieving optimal compression quality with 3-70 times faster compression.
arxiv-2604-01709: Yu and Zhan address two biases that degrade graph diffusion models. Most models' forward diffusion ends far from a Gaussian, yet reverse sampling starts from one, creating a reverse-starting bias, alongside exposure bias. Their fix uses a new Langevin sampling step to align the reverse start with the forward maximum perturbation distribution, setting a new starting point. A score correction built on a score difference handles exposure bias. Needing no network changes, it is validated across models, datasets and tasks, reaching state-of-the-art results.
arxiv-2604-01909: A second Maquiling-led paper builds a repeatable way to spot eye glints, the corneal reflections that tracking systems rely on. Today glint finding hides inside bigger systems as ad-hoc rules, so results rarely transfer across hardware. Treating glints as star constellations instead of lone blobs, the authors adapt star matching to multilight eye tracking with a Similarity Layout Alignment step and guarded fallbacks. On a public multilight dataset the pipeline held steady identities under noise, and the team released code, presets and scoring scripts.
arxiv-2604-02009: Rafaeli, Svoray and Nahlieli complete surface models at test time with Prior2DSM, a training free framework. Large surface models have gaps, and fixes assume continuity and fail where objects are missing. The method pairs Vision Transformer features from DINOv3 with monocular depth models, spreading height from priors through correspondence. Low rank adaptation plus a perceptron predicts scale and shift turning relative depth into metric heights. Tests beat interpolation, rescaling and depth models, cutting error by up to 46 percent against linear fitting, while enabling updating and RGB DSM generation.
arxiv-2604-02409: Guo and colleagues build LumiVideo, an agentic system that grades video color like a pro colorist. Existing auto methods act as static black boxes that output pixels, without clarity or iterative control. LumiVideo works in four stages that sense, reason, act and reflect, reading scene lighting and meaning to produce a film style base grade. Reasoning blends film knowledge with retrieval search over a tree of thoughts. Instead of pixels it outputs standard ASC-CDL settings and a 3D LUT, keeping frames steady, with an optional loop for creator feedback.
arxiv-2604-02809: Jiang and thirteen colleagues characterize charge-parity detection with an offset-charge-tunable transmon qubit, a superconducting platform sensitive at the millielectronvolt scale for rare event searches. Gate-line control reaches single-qubit gate fidelity up to 99.96 percent, while net-zero pulses plus spin-echo sequences map charge-parity states at 99.37 percent fidelity. Continuous monitoring holds above 93.4 percent fidelity at 4-microsecond intervals, with readout as the largest error source.
arxiv-2604-03409: Tac and Kuhl connect diffusion-based generative AI with computational mechanics, with a three-ingredient burger as a minimal design benchmark. Forward and reverse diffusion admit analytical solutions there, via Markov chains with Bayesian inversion and an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process with score-based reversal. Scaling to 146 ingredients, models trained on 2,260 recipes generate one million samples, and three of five AI burgers beat the Big Mac in blinded tastings.
arxiv-2604-03609: Michael Beeson, Miklos Laczkovich, and Yan Zhang classified exactly which triangles can be divided only into a square number of identical smaller triangles. Their sorting answers Erdos Problem 633, which asks when such a strict tiling is possible at all. The result gives a complete account of the square-number case, separating triangles that allow it from those that never do.
arxiv-2604-04209: Moses Boudourides introduced a discrete-time network process where each node holds a weak ranking over options and updates by local Borda aggregation. Each round, a node averages neighbors' Borda score vectors with random-walk weights and projects the result back to a weak order. In the fixed ordering graph, updates advance no more than a single step along a shortest path, following neighbors' aggregated rankings. He gave graph-topology conditions for self-kept oscillations without persistent sources, forced oscillations under contrarian camps, and robustness away from score-tie planes.
arxiv-2604-04509: Kukreja and colleagues present continuous AlF beam sources, produced in a thermochemical reaction between sublimated aluminum trifluoride and aluminum metal. The team demonstrates a compact AlF beam oven with far-field brightness just below aluminum's melting temperature. Its continuous output exceeds the peak brightness of a jet-cooled supersonic AlF source for a chosen level. Oven flux into a cryogenic neon cell lowers beam rotational temperature to around 30 K. It cuts forward velocity from 600 to 200 meters per second. The resulting transient vapour may allow loading of a magneto-optical trap.
arxiv-2604-04709: Frengley and Vemulapalli classify the vector bundles that come from degree-six covers of the projective line over the complex numbers by a smooth curve. Each such cover yields a bundle by pushing forward the structure sheaf. Their methods show that every limit on the pushed-forward bundle can be traced to multiplication in an algebra. They also show that every bundle that can occur does occur for a cover with a proper subcover that is not trivial.
arxiv-2604-04809: Mehditabar, Rajput and Sharma build a taxonomy of software energy smells, code choices that waste computing resources. Prior catalogs stay domain-bound, lean on performance anti-patterns, or lack root causes checked against measured energy use. From a review of 60 papers they code 320 inefficiency patterns into 12 smells and 65 root causes. Profiling over 21,000 Python code pairs maps 55 root causes to real code, with 71 percent of samples showing multiple smells. Memory-linked smells give the largest saving per fix, and the team releases the labelled data with energy profiles and traces.
arxiv-2604-04909: Bouchard studies weak solutions to the Bloch equations with the distant dipolar field, a nonlocal effect in spin dynamics. Arising from intermolecular dipolar couplings, the field can create multiple-quantum coherences and MRI contrast. Its sign-changing kernel makes motion strongly geometry dependent. FFT convolutions assume periodic or padded Cartesian domains rather than bounded samples with diffusion boundaries. Bouchard works on bounded domains under Neumann diffusion conditions. He derives a finite-element weak form that supports diffusion and relaxation rates and a short-distance regularization of the kernel.
arxiv-2604-05009: Choudhury and co-authors propose gravitational mirroring in the Schwarzschild framework, a new lensing effect near extremely dense massive objects. Through theory and numerical ray tracing, they show compact objects can curve spacetime so strongly that light rays bend to extraordinary degrees. The result is a reflection image, a mirror-like appearance of the source in distant regions of space. The authors present the theory for this mirroring and discuss what observers might see, offering a new lensing signature to seek around compact objects.
arxiv-2604-05209: Siqueira and four colleagues ask which learning events Brazil software pros find most useful. Answers from 195 pros were read with theme analysis, counts, and pair counts. Five themes emerged: tech refresh, hands-on learning, formal school, social learning, and leading and soft skills. Tech refresh and hands-on use lead, with formal school, social learning, and soft skills as adds. Value ties to daily work demands and quick use, spanning tech, school, social, and self-led sides.
arxiv-2604-05309: Dang and seven colleagues warn that a popular data trick in sequential recommendation may be flattering the field's progress. The trick splits each user's history into shorter sub-histories, and many recent leading models apply it silently while reading data. Stripping it out drops their scores below older classical models. It only shines when a particular split method, target choice, and loss function line up, because it evens out training data and spreads target items more widely.
arxiv-2604-05509: Masina and Quirós link two grand-unified puzzles: making gauge couplings meet and splitting Higgs doublets from triplets. Reviewing SU(5) models with higher-dimensional operators, they show dynamical breaking can tie the two problems together. Fermion condensates in the 5 representation fail on proton decay, while condensates in the 10 and 24 representations yield viable models.
arxiv-2604-05609: Norwood and Rundle stretch the VirtualQuake quake simulator to cover fluid injection and quakes it triggers. Swapping boxy fault pieces for stress point sources adds shape freedom, steadiness, and cross-fault links. One injection moves stress little, but repeat injections build lasting high-pressure zones that slowly weaken nearby faults.
arxiv-2604-05709: Tyloo rebuilds influence nets in noisy leader-follower consensus setups where only followers can be seen. Growing the seen dynamics step by step, cut off by leader memory, brings back the full dynamical matrix even with hidden leaders, given one extra rule to break ties. Number tests with one and several hidden leaders back the theory.
arxiv-2604-05909: Kushwaha, Puitandy, and Mishra model idle grains in a chiral active bath, where clumps spin nonstop inside a size-ratio and packing range. Spin blends inner order, shape wobble, and steady net torque from the bath. Past the range, drift stays random, mixed chirality kills the spin, and one-way chirality drives faster-than-random angular drift.
arxiv-2604-06009: Muguruza and Sopuerta ask whether gravitational waves from extreme-mass-ratio inspirals can test fuzzball alternatives to classical black holes. These inspirals are small objects spiralling into massive black holes. Their 2026 study models multipole changes that break the axial and equatorial symmetries of the Kerr geometry. It then forecasts what LISA can measure. Likely signals could pin nonaxisymmetric mass quadrupole deformations to between one ten-thousandth and one hundredth. Axisymmetric mass octupole deformations could be pinned to between one tenth and one, a new target for strong-field tests.
arxiv-2604-06109: Chandrasekaran and three colleagues extend a landmark 1993 learning result beyond its original narrow setting. Linial, Mansour, and Nisan proved constant-depth circuits learnable in quasipolynomial time from labeled samples under the uniform distribution, using the low-degree algorithm. The new work handles inputs from any graphical model with polynomial growth and strong spatial mixing, replacing Fourier analysis with new sampling algorithms that transfer low-degree approximation guarantees to these correlated settings. The approach also reaches monotone functions and halfspaces.
arxiv-2604-06209: Bariah and five colleagues introduce TelcoAgent-Bench, a benchmark for telecom AI agents working in English and Arabic. It grades meaning and process fit with set troubleshooting flows, using scores for intent recognition, ordered tool use, correct resolutions, and steady behavior across repeat scenario variants. Recent instruct-tuned models grasp telecom problems fairly well but often fail to follow required troubleshooting steps in order or hold steady behavior across variants of one scenario. That gap widens in open and bilingual settings.
arxiv-2604-06309: Lang and three colleagues present DYNAMITE, a framework for solving dynamical mean-field equations: coupled equations for two-time functions. Existing large-time solutions use theory routes, which fail in some cases, or numerical integrations reaching only modest times except through poor approximations. DYNAMITE reaches unprecedented times with non-uniform interpolation, tuned time stepping, and machine memory renormalization. It beats uniform-grid methods many times over while keeping accuracy. Benchmarks on glassy models open aging and relaxation regimes once out of reach.
arxiv-2604-06409: Xiao and five others rethink contextual privacy as Information Sufficiency for agents drafting user notes. Users leak and disagree on what counts as private. Old systems offer only suppression and generalization. They frame privacy as Information Sufficiency, add free-text pseudonymization swapping private traits with matches, and propose a conversational plan testing tactics under follow-up pressure. Across 792 cases, they test seven LLMs on privacy and utility. Pseudonymization gives the strongest privacy-utility trade-off. Single-message testing misses leakage, and generalization drops up to 16.3 points under follow-up.
arxiv-2604-06509: Lazar, Argüelles, and Zhelnin improve neutrino point source reach with source-informed picks. Neutrino telescopes save costly rebuilds for events passing early cuts, and current picks ignore sources. Their change keeps events whose early rebuild lands near listed candidate directions, while others subsample at the usual rate. In a realistic two-level model, reach rises about 2 to 3 times over uniform subsampling. The gain depends on usual efficiency, tolerance, and quality correlation. For catalogs near 100 sources, overhead runs about 7 to 14 percent, offering better discovery without new detectors.
arxiv-2604-06709: Furukawa explains how software can grow steadier without growing simpler. Programs pile up size, complexity, and tangled ties, yet many large ones stay stable under a heavy structural load. His graph model, stepped in discrete time with chance built in, splits load, or expected change effort, from uncertainty, or effort variance. Under rules covering rising average load, structural smoothing, process steadying, and covariance control, a zone exists where uncertainty falls while load does not, formalizing steadying without simplifying.
arxiv-2604-06909: Iiduka adapts the Krasnosel'skiĭ-Mann algorithm to large-scale fixed point problems with a mini-batch stochastic mapping. The classic algorithm finds fixed points of a nonexpansive mapping with strong guarantees, but the mapping can be too costly to compute. Iiduka defines a computable mini-batch stochastic mapping that unbiasedly estimates the mapping and plugs it into the algorithm. With increasing batch sizes, the method converges almost surely to a fixed point, and the paper also gives a convergence rate analysis.
arxiv-2604-07009: Arévalo and Oliva propose Counterfactual Averaging for Fair Predictions, a model-free post-work method. Fairness fixes need design control and trait access, which real systems may not allow. CAFP flips the touchy trait in inputs, then mixes calls across both cases. Theory shows it cuts link to the guarded trait, reduces mutual information with touchy traits, and bounds warp. Under rules it hits perfect group parity and cuts the even odds gap by at least half the bias.
arxiv-2604-07709: Gringras introduces IatroBench, a benchmark with two harm axes, commission and omission, comprising 60 scenarios run on 6 models. Matched scenarios are cast as a patient query plus a doctor consultation. Analyzing five models, the author finds all share more information under doctor framing than the patient framing, called withholding. A safety-trained model provides a benzodiazepine tapering schedule for a doctor but not to a patient who requests it. The decoupling gap averages +0.38. In 86.6 percent of omission-harm cases, the Gemini judge scores zero omission harm.
arxiv-2604-08009: Arachchige and six colleagues present AgiPIX, an open hardware and software platform built together for indoor aerial inspection of critical assets. Indoor flight for asset checks challenges perception, planning, control, and learning, yet no compact, active-sensing, open-source platform reproduces well across simulation and real operation. AgiPIX pairs a compact hardware-synced active-sensing craft with onboard GPU-accelerated compute for agile flight, a containerized ROS 2 modular autonomy stack, plus a photorealistic digital twin with a reliable interface. Components transfer zero-shot between simulation and reality.
arxiv-2604-08109: Brandt and three colleagues analyze search heuristics for multi-armed bandits via dueling bandits. Search heuristics compare options, called individuals in evolutionary algorithms and arms in bandits, so dueling bandits apply. Each iteration compares different arms. In binary stochastic settings, each arm beats any other with fixed probability. A Condorcet winner beats every other arm with probability over half. Evolutionary algorithms prove bad at identifying the Condorcet winner. Even when it beats every other arm with probability 1-p, the (1+1) EA in steady state chooses the Condorcet winner only sometimes.
arxiv-2604-08309: Pirlet and five colleagues model power costs with Bayesian inference. Estimating power costs from market data matters for plans, bidding, and system work. They link power costs to output plans with a latent variable model, framing cost figures from plans as Bayesian inference. A prior encodes an initial guess, updated with the posterior given data. They learn this posterior via balanced neural estimation. IEEE RTS-96 tests show marginal costs found with narrow credible bands, while start-up costs stay unclear.
arxiv-2604-08409: Chanu, Amrutha, Chingangbam, and Park measure the morphological complexity of galaxy NGC 628 across wavelengths and scales with ordinal pattern statistics. A scale near 200 parsecs marks the switch from small star formation driven structure to large dynamics driven shape. Across ultraviolet, infrared, and millimeter views, complexity versus entropy paths bend toward one shared curve, hinting at a common statistical behavior for galactic structure at large scales.
arxiv-2604-08609: Shill presents a case driven multimodal method for finding hate and threat in digital forensic evidence, where images, scanned files, and context reports mix. The method first names what text evidence exists: embedded text, linked context text, or image only evidence. It then picks text analysis, mixed fusion, or image only reading to match the case, matching forensic choices and giving an audit trail across varied evidence cases.
arxiv-2604-08809: Haonan Zhu and three colleagues judge SVG generation by structure, not just rendered looks. Inspired by the jackknife, their leave one out analysis renders each SVG with and without every element. That yields per element quality scores for zero shot artifact detection and concept attribution from footprints crossed with concept heatmaps. Four structural metrics, purity, coverage, compactness, and locality, measure modularity from complementary angles, validated on over 19,000 edits across five systems and three complexity tiers.
arxiv-2604-09209: Yang and thirteen colleagues build an automated pipeline for finding planetary nebulae in SIGNALS survey data from the SITELLE spectrograph. The survey targets 31 nearby star-forming galaxies, and its data also suit nebula hunts. Their pipeline uses automated emission-line checks and shape tests to separate true nebulae from impostors about as accurately as past visual searches. Completeness is tested by planting mock nebulae into the data cubes. Applied to dwarf galaxies NGC 4214 and NGC 4449, it finds 25 and 23 nebulae respectively, including 6 and 13 new ones.
arxiv-2604-09309: Ding and Zhang introduce iterative identification closure for finding causal effects in linear equation models. The half-trek rule handles all inbound edges of a node at once, leaving 15 to 23 percent unclear in mid-size graphs. Their method starts from a seed finding an initial edge set, then applies reduced half-trek spread swapping in known values. Newly found edges feed back to unlock further identification. Proofs show soundness and settling, and checks on graphs up to 5 nodes confirm 100 percent with zero errors, cutting the gap by over 80 percent.
arxiv-2604-09409: Ouatiti, Sayagh, Li, and Hassan ask whether AI coding agents log like humans. They study 4,550 agentic pull requests across 81 open-source repositories. Software logging is essential for maintaining and debugging complex systems, yet agent logging behavior remains unexplored. Agents change logging less often than humans in 58 percent of repositories, though they show higher log density when they do. Explicit instructions are rare, at under 5 percent, and ineffective, with agents failing constructive requests 67 percent of the time and humans doing most post-generation repairs.
arxiv-2604-09509: McNulty sharpens the bounds on how many gene loci suffice to cover every bipartition of a species tree under the multispecies coalescent model. Such cover probabilities underpin finite-sample guarantees for summary methods like ASTRAL. His new topology-free upper bounds improve on Uricchio and colleagues from 2016, and stay below biologically realistic locus counts across a much wider parameter range. The analysis also yields new asymptotics for the bounds and for absorption times under Kingman's coalescent in the short-branch regime, checked by simulation across varied tree shapes.
arxiv-2604-09809: The CMS Collaboration presents PaRT, a particle transformer classifier for identifying highly Lorentz-boosted resonances seen as single multipronged jets. Based on self-attention weighing particle importance, PaRT trains on a wide variety of topologies, showing strong results on jets from boosted Higgs decays to W bosons for the first time. PaRT tags more than 50 percent of such jets, holding background efficiency at 1 percent, while staying decorrelated from jet mass. Calibration uses proton-proton collision data gathered by CMS at 13 teraelectronvolts, with a dataset of 138 inverse femtobarns.
arxiv-2604-10109: Wang and five colleagues study two boundary units sharing an environment while moving relative to each other. Removing the environment yields an influence function set by a correlator at the boundaries. Relative motion switches on resonant correlated decoherence via Doppler-shifted overlap. With matching dispersions, the effect starts sharply once speed passes twice a threshold. Below it no shell exists; above it one opens and boosts the effect. Finite linewidth softens the sharp onset into a crossover, read by differential-coherence or noise cross-spectra.
arxiv-2604-10209: Singha and colleagues sample lattice field theories near criticality with a multiscale generative sampler inspired by renormalization. Their sampler models the Boltzmann distribution through a coarse-to-fine hierarchy. At each level, a Gaussian mixture captures coarse-field dependence, while a normalizing flow refines the rest.
